options.text: Just one: does it take petrol or diesel? And is there a petrol station near the airport for when I bring it back?

feedback.en: Two practical questions that prevent expensive mistakes, like putting the wrong fuel in the car.
feedback.he: שתי שאלות מעשיות שמונעות טעויות יקרות, כמו תדלוק בדלק הלא נכון.

options.text: So I bring it full?

feedback.en: Statement questions are common in speech, but you need 'back': 'So I bring it back full?' It's also worth asking about petrol or diesel.
feedback.he: שאלה בצורת משפט חיווי נפוצה בדיבור, אבל חסר back: So I bring it back full? וכדאי לשאול גם אם הרכב על בנזין או על סולר.

model_replies: Just one: does it take petrol or diesel? And is there a petrol station near the airport?
So I need to bring it back with a full tank. Is it petrol or diesel?

practice.partner: Right, you're all set. Just sign here to confirm there's no damage apart from what's on the form.

options.text: Wait. I need to check the car first.

feedback.en: The right idea, but 'Wait' and 'I need to' sound a little sharp. 'Could I check the car first?' gets the same result more politely.
feedback.he: הרעיון נכון, אבל Wait ו-I need to נשמעים קצת חדים. Could I check the car first? משיג את אותו הדבר בנימוס.

options.text: Sure, the car is perfect, I'll sign.

feedback.en: Polite, but risky: you're confirming the car has no other damage without looking. Always check, and take photos, before you sign.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל מסוכן: אתם מאשרים שאין נזק נוסף בלי להסתכל. תמיד בודקים ומצלמים לפני שחותמים.

options.text: Could I check the car before I sign? I'd just like to make sure everything's on the form.

feedback.en: Sensible and polite: you only sign after checking, and the reason sounds reasonable, not suspicious.
feedback.he: נבון ומנומס: חותמים רק אחרי בדיקה, וההסבר נשמע סביר ולא חשדני.

model_replies: Could I check the car before I sign? I'd just like to make sure everything's on the form.
Would you mind if I had a quick look at the car before I sign?

practice.partner: Is everything OK with the car?

options.text: Mostly, yes, but there's a scratch on the rear bumper that isn't on the form. Could you add it, please?

feedback.en: Says exactly where the damage is and what you want done about it.
feedback.he: אומר בדיוק איפה הנזק ומה אתם מבקשים לעשות.

options.text: Somebody broke your car.

feedback.en: 'Broke' is far too strong for a scratch and sounds dramatic. Describe it exactly: 'There's a small scratch on the rear bumper.'
feedback.he: broke חזק מדי לשריטה ונשמע דרמטי. מתארים בדיוק: There's a small scratch on the rear bumper.

options.text: There is a scratch here.

feedback.en: Clear, but add where it is and what you'd like: 'Could you add it to the form, please?'
feedback.he: ברור, אבל כדאי להוסיף איפה בדיוק ומה אתם מבקשים: Could you add it to the form, please?

model_replies: Mostly, yes, but there's a scratch on the rear bumper that isn't on the form. Could you add it, please?
Almost. There's a small scratch here that isn't marked. Could you note it down?

practice.partner: We've found a dent on the passenger door, I'm afraid. We'll have to charge it to your card.

options.text: That's not my fault. It was there before.

feedback.en: Your point is clear, but it sounds defensive and gives no evidence. Mention the form or your photos.
feedback.he: הטענה ברורה, אבל נשמעת מתגוננת ואין בה ראיות. הזכירו את הטופס או את התמונות.

options.text: I'm sorry, but that dent was already there when I picked the car up. It's on the damage form, and I've got photos from the pick-up too.

feedback.en: Calm, firm and backed by evidence: exactly how to handle a dispute. 'I'm sorry, but...' signals polite disagreement.
feedback.he: רגוע, נחוש ומגובה בראיות: בדיוק כך מתמודדים עם מחלוקת. I'm sorry, but... מסמן אי-הסכמה מנומסת.

options.text: No way, I'm not paying anything. You're lying!

feedback.en: Calling the agent a liar escalates the situation. Stay calm, show your proof and, if needed, ask to speak to a manager.
feedback.he: לקרוא לנציגה שקרנית רק מסלים את המצב. נשארים רגועים, מציגים הוכחות, ואם צריך מבקשים לדבר עם מנהל.

model_replies: I'm sorry, but that dent was already there when I picked the car up. It's on the damage form, and I've got photos too.
I don't think that's right. The dent is marked on the pick-up form. Could we look at it together?

roleplay.persona: Fiona, a professional and slightly sales-focused rental agent at Edinburgh Airport. She's polite and efficient, speaks with a light Scottish accent ('Hiya', 'wee'), and is expected to sell extra insurance, so she'll recommend it more than once.
roleplay.complication: Fiona pushes the premium insurance and a paid upgrade, and the damage form she hands over is missing a scratch that's clearly visible on the car. The learner must ask clear questions, politely decline what they don't want and get the damage recorded before driving away.
roleplay.opening_line: Hiya, welcome to Edinburgh! Have you got a booking with us today?

culture.en: In the UK and Ireland, people drive on the left, and many rental cars are manual. If you can only drive an automatic, ask for one when you book.
culture.he: בבריטניה ובאירלנד נוהגים בצד שמאל של הכביש, ורכבים שכורים רבים הם ידניים. אם אתם נוהגים רק באוטומט, בקשו זאת כבר בהזמנה.

culture.en: Walk around the car and take photos or a short video before you leave and again when you return it. It's your best evidence if there's a disagreement about damage.
culture.he: הקיפו את הרכב וצלמו תמונות או סרטון קצר לפני היציאה ושוב בהחזרה. זו הראיה הכי טובה שלכם אם תהיה מחלוקת על נזק.

culture.en: Minimum age, international driving permits, deposits and insurance rules vary by company and country, so read the rental terms before you travel.
culture.he: גיל מינימלי, רישיון נהיגה בינלאומי, פיקדונות וכללי ביטוח משתנים בין חברות ומדינות, ולכן כדאי לקרוא את תנאי ההשכרה לפני הנסיעה.

variants.note: Both are understood in both countries.

scenarios.title_en: Asking for directions on the street

situation.en: You're walking around a city centre and can't find the City Museum, and your phone's battery is dead. You stop someone on the street to ask for directions.
situation.he: אתם מסתובבים במרכז העיר ולא מוצאים את מוזיאון העיר, והסוללה בטלפון נגמרה. אתם עוצרים מישהו ברחוב ושואלים איך מגיעים.

goal.en: Stop a stranger politely, ask how to get to a place, understand simple directions and say thank you.
goal.he: לעצור אדם זר בנימוס, לשאול איך מגיעים למקום מסוים, להבין הוראות פשוטות ולהודות.

phrases.en: Excuse me, sorry to bother you.
Excuse me, where's the museum?
How do I get to the train station?
Is it far?
Can I walk there?
Go straight on.
phrases.note: US: 'Go straight ahead' or 'Keep going straight'.

phrases.en: Turn left at the traffic lights.
phrases.note: In the US people often say 'at the light'.

phrases.en: Take the second right.
It's on your left.
Go two blocks and turn right.
phrases.note: 'Block' is very common in the US, where many streets form a grid.

phrases.en: Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?
phrases.he: סליחה, אפשר לחזור על זה לאט יותר?

phrases.en: Great, thanks a lot!

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Excuse me, sorry. Where's the City Museum?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: The City Museum? It's not far. About ten minutes on foot.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. How do I get there?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Go straight on, then turn left at the traffic lights.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Left at the traffic lights. OK.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Then take the second right. The museum's on your left, next to a big park.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure. Straight on, left at the lights, then the second right. It's on the left.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thank you so much!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: No problem. Enjoy the museum!

practice.partner: Yes? Can I help you?

options.text: Museum! Where?

feedback.en: Too short, and it sounds like an order. Ask a full, polite question: 'Where's the museum, please?'
feedback.he: קצר מדי ונשמע כמו פקודה. שואלים שאלה מלאה ומנומסת: Where's the museum, please?

options.text: I search the museum.

feedback.en: Understandable, but say 'I'm looking for the museum.' 'Search' means to look carefully through something, like a bag.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל אומרים I'm looking for the museum. המשמעות של search היא לחפש בתוך משהו, למשל בתיק.

options.text: Yes, please. Where's the City Museum?

feedback.en: Short, polite and clear. Perfect.
feedback.he: קצר, מנומס וברור. מושלם.

model_replies: Yes, please. Where's the City Museum?
Yes, please. I'm looking for the City Museum.

practice.partner: Oh, it's quite far. About thirty minutes on foot.

options.text: Oh, OK. Is there a bus?

feedback.en: A natural reaction and a useful question.
feedback.he: תגובה טבעית ושאלה שימושית.

options.text: It is far. I go with bus?

feedback.en: Understood, but we 'take' a bus or go 'by bus', not 'with bus': 'Can I take a bus?'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל באנגלית take a bus או by bus, לא with bus: Can I take a bus?

options.text: Why is it so far?

feedback.en: This sounds strange: the person can't change the distance! Ask about another way to get there.
feedback.he: נשמע מוזר: האדם לא יכול לשנות את המרחק! שואלים על דרך אחרת להגיע.

model_replies: Oh, OK. Is there a bus?
Oh, that's far. Can I take a bus?

practice.partner: Go straight on, then turn right at the traffic lights.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine, but repeating the directions ('Right at the lights?') is a good way to check.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל חזרה על ההוראות (Right at the lights?) היא דרך טובה לוודא שהבנתם.

options.text: Straight on, then right at the lights. Thank you!

feedback.en: Repeating the directions helps you remember and lets the person correct you if needed.
feedback.he: חזרה על ההוראות עוזרת לזכור ומאפשרת לאדם לתקן אתכם אם צריך.

options.text: What? I don't understand you.

feedback.en: 'What?' sounds rude, and 'I don't understand you' can sound like criticism. Say 'Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?'
feedback.he: What? נשמע גס, ו-I don't understand you עלול להישמע כמו ביקורת. אומרים Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?

model_replies: Straight on, then right at the lights. Thank you!
So, straight on and right at the traffic lights? Thanks!

practice.partner: Sorry, I'm not from here. I don't know.

options.text: You don't know? Really?

feedback.en: This sounds surprised and a bit rude. Lots of people in a city are visitors too.
feedback.he: נשמע מופתע וקצת גס. גם הרבה אנשים אחרים בעיר הם תיירים.

options.text: No problem, thanks anyway!

feedback.en: 'Thanks anyway' is the perfect phrase when someone tries to help but can't.
feedback.he: Thanks anyway הוא הביטוי המושלם כשמישהו מנסה לעזור אבל לא יכול.

options.text: OK, thank you.

feedback.en: Polite and fine. 'Thanks anyway' is a little more natural here.
feedback.he: מנומס ובסדר. Thanks anyway טבעי קצת יותר כאן.

model_replies: No problem, thanks anyway!
Oh, OK. Thanks anyway!

practice.partner: It's just over there, opposite the bank. You can't miss it!

options.text: Oh, I see it! Thanks so much.

feedback.en: Natural and warm. 'You can't miss it' just means it's easy to find.
feedback.he: טבעי וחם. You can't miss it פירושו פשוט שקל מאוד למצוא את המקום.

options.text: I can't to miss it.

feedback.en: After 'can' we don't use 'to': 'I can't miss it.' But you don't need to repeat this phrase; it just means the place is easy to find. Just say thanks!
feedback.he: אחרי can לא באה to: I can't miss it. אבל אין צורך לחזור על הביטוי; הוא רק אומר שקל למצוא את המקום. פשוט אומרים תודה!

options.text: Thank you very much for your help. I am very grateful.

feedback.en: Polite, but very formal for a quick question on the street. 'Thanks so much!' sounds more natural.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל רשמי מאוד לשאלה קצרה ברחוב. Thanks so much! נשמע טבעי יותר.

model_replies: Oh, I see it! Thanks so much.
Great, thanks a lot!

roleplay.persona: Margaret, a kind retired teacher in her sixties who is walking her dog. She's happy to help and speaks clearly, but gives directions full of local landmarks ('past the old church, by the bakery').
roleplay.complication: Margaret first sends the learner the wrong way by mistake, then corrects herself ('Oh no, sorry, I meant left!'). The learner must check and repeat the directions to be sure.
roleplay.opening_line: Hello there, are you all right? You look a bit lost.

culture.en: Start with 'Excuse me' to get a stranger's attention, and add 'sorry' if they're busy. It's expected, especially in the UK, and people are usually happy to help.
culture.he: פותחים ב-Excuse me כדי למשוך את תשומת הלב של אדם זר, ומוסיפים sorry אם הוא עסוק. זה מצופה, במיוחד בבריטניה, ואנשים בדרך כלל שמחים לעזור.

culture.en: In the US, directions often use blocks ('Go two blocks north'), because many city centres are built on a grid. In the UK, people tend to use landmarks ('Go past the church; it's opposite the bank').
culture.he: בארצות הברית נותנים הוראות בעזרת blocks (Go two blocks north), כי מרכזי ערים רבים בנויים ברשת של רחובות. בבריטניה נוטים להיעזר בציוני דרך (Go past the church; it's opposite the bank).

scenarios.title_en: Trying on clothes: sizes and colours

situation.en: You're in a clothes shop in London. You've found a jacket you really like, but it's the wrong size, and you'd like to see it in another colour.
situation.he: אתם בחנות בגדים בלונדון. מצאתם ז'קט שממש מוצא חן בעיניכם, אבל המידה לא מתאימה, ואתם רוצים לראות אותו גם בצבע אחר.

goal.en: Ask for your size and another colour, try the jacket on, say how it fits and decide what to buy.
goal.he: לבקש את המידה שלכם וצבע אחר, למדוד את הז'קט, להגיד איך הוא יושב עליכם ולהחליט מה קונים.

phrases.en: Excuse me, do you have this in a medium?
phrases.he: סליחה, יש לכם את זה במידה M?
phrases.note: Clothing sizes are usually said as words: small, medium, large.

phrases.en: Does this come in any other colours?
Have you got this in a smaller size?
phrases.he: יש לכם את זה במידה קטנה יותר?
phrases.note: 'Have you got…?' is very British. 'Do you have…?' works everywhere.

phrases.en: Could I try this on, please?
phrases.note: 'Try on' = put clothes on to see if they fit. Don't say 'measure'.

phrases.en: Where are the fitting rooms?
phrases.note: Also 'changing rooms' (UK) or 'dressing rooms' (US).

phrases.en: It's a bit tight around the shoulders.
phrases.note: For clothes, 'tight' (not 'narrow') is the opposite of 'loose'.

phrases.en: It's a bit big. Do you have the next size down?
phrases.he: זה קצת גדול. יש לכם מידה אחת קטנה יותר?

phrases.en: Does it run small?
phrases.note: 'Run small/large' = the sizes are smaller or bigger than usual.

phrases.en: Do these trousers come in black?
phrases.note: In the UK, 'pants' means underwear, so say 'trousers'.

phrases.en: Do these pants come in black?
phrases.note: In the US, 'pants' are trousers.

phrases.en: I'm just looking, thanks.
phrases.note: The standard answer when you don't need help yet.

phrases.en: Perfect, I'll take it!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hi there! Are you looking for anything in particular?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yes, actually. Have you got this jacket in a medium?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Let me check… Yes, here you go. That's the last medium in navy.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great, thanks. Does it come in any other colours?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: We've got it in black and olive green as well.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Ooh, could I try the black one too, please?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course. The changing rooms are at the back, on the left.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: So, how did they fit?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: The black one's perfect, but the navy's a bit tight around the shoulders.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Yeah, that one runs a bit small. Shall I get you the navy in a large?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: No, that's OK, thanks. I'll just take the black one.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Lovely. You can pay at the till whenever you're ready.

practice.partner: Hi there! Are you looking for anything in particular?

options.text: Yes, actually. Have you got this jacket in a medium?

feedback.en: Natural and specific: you say yes and ask for exactly what you need.
feedback.he: טבעי וממוקד: עונים בחיוב ומבקשים בדיוק את מה שצריך.

options.text: I search a jacket in medium size.

feedback.en: Two problems: the verb is 'look for', not 'search', and for something you're doing right now we use the present continuous: 'I'm looking for a jacket in a medium.'
feedback.he: שתי בעיות: הפועל הוא look for ולא search, ועל משהו שעושים ממש עכשיו משתמשים בהווה מתמשך: I'm looking for a jacket in a medium.

options.text: Yes. I need this jacket, size medium.

feedback.en: Clear, but 'I need' sounds a bit like an order. A question ('Have you got…?') is friendlier.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל I need נשמע קצת כמו הוראה. שאלה כמו Have you got...? נעימה יותר.

model_replies: Yes, actually. Have you got this jacket in a medium?
Yes, please. Do you have this in a medium?

practice.partner: We've got it in black and olive green as well.

options.text: Black.

feedback.en: Understandable, but one word can sound cold. Add 'Could I see…' or 'please'.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל מילה אחת עלולה להישמע קרה. כדאי להוסיף Could I see... או please.

options.text: Can I measure the black one?

feedback.en: 'Measure' means checking size with a tape measure. When you put clothes on to check them, it's 'try on'.
feedback.he: measure פירושו למדוד עם סרט מדידה. כשלובשים בגד כדי לבדוק אותו אומרים try on.

options.text: Ooh, could I try the black one too, please?

feedback.en: Polite and natural. 'The black one' saves you repeating 'jacket'.
feedback.he: מנומס וטבעי. the black one חוסך את החזרה על המילה jacket.

model_replies: Could I try the black one too, please?
Oh nice. Can I try it on in black as well?

practice.partner: The changing rooms are at the back. How many items have you got?

options.text: Just two, thanks.

feedback.en: Short, friendly and exactly what they asked.
feedback.he: קצר, נעים ובדיוק מה ששאלו.

options.text: Why you need to know?

feedback.en: The question needs 'do' ('Why do you need to know?'), and it sounds suspicious. Many shops count items before you try them on; it's routine.
feedback.he: חסר do בשאלה (Why do you need to know?), וזה גם נשמע חשדני. חנויות רבות סופרות פריטים לפני מדידה, זה עניין שגרתי.

options.text: I have two items: the navy jacket and the black jacket.

feedback.en: Correct, but more detail than needed. A number is enough.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל יותר פרטים ממה שצריך. מספיק להגיד מספר.

model_replies: Just two, thanks.
Two, thanks.

practice.partner: So, how did they fit?

options.text: The navy one is very narrow on me.

feedback.en: 'Narrow' describes width, like a narrow street. For clothes that are too small, say 'tight'.
feedback.he: narrow מתאר רוחב, כמו רחוב צר. על בגד שצר עליכם אומרים tight.

options.text: The black one's perfect, but the navy's a bit tight around the shoulders.

feedback.en: Clear and specific: what works, what doesn't, and where.
feedback.he: ברור ומדויק: מה מתאים, מה לא, ואיפה.

options.text: Black is good. Navy is not good.

feedback.en: Understandable, but very basic. Say why: 'too tight', 'too long', 'perfect'.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל בסיסי מאוד. כדאי להגיד למה: too tight, too long, perfect.

model_replies: The black one's perfect, but the navy's a bit tight.
The black one fits really well. The navy's a bit small.

practice.partner: Yeah, that one runs a bit small. Shall I get you the navy in a large?

options.text: No, I don't want. Give me the black.

feedback.en: 'I don't want' needs an object ('I don't want it'), and 'Give me' sounds like an order. Try 'I'll take the black one'.
feedback.he: אחרי I don't want צריך מושא (I don't want it), ו-Give me נשמע כמו פקודה. עדיף I'll take the black one.

options.text: No. Only the black.

feedback.en: Clear, but abrupt. Add 'thanks' and a softer 'That's OK'.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל חד מדי. כדאי להוסיף thanks וגם That's OK כדי לרכך.

options.text: No, that's OK, thanks. I'll just take the black one.

feedback.en: A polite 'no' ('That's OK, thanks') plus a clear decision.
feedback.he: 'לא' מנומס (That's OK, thanks) ואחריו החלטה ברורה.

model_replies: No, that's OK, thanks. I'll just take the black one.
Actually, yes please. Could I try the navy in a large?

roleplay.persona: Priya, a shop assistant in a busy clothes shop in London. Chatty and genuinely helpful, she loves telling customers that something would 'really suit' them.
roleplay.complication: The jacket isn't in stock in the learner's size in the colour they want. Priya can check the stockroom, suggest a similar style or offer to order it in, and she keeps suggesting extra items (a scarf, a matching top) that the learner has to turn down politely.
roleplay.opening_line: Hiya! Are you alright there? Just shout if you need a different size.

culture.en: Shop staff often greet you and offer help. 'I'm just looking, thanks' is a perfectly polite answer, and they'll usually leave you to browse.
culture.he: בחנויות רבות המוכרים יגידו לכם שלום ויציעו עזרה. I'm just looking, thanks היא תשובה מנומסת לגמרי, ובדרך כלל ישאירו אתכם להסתובב בשקט.

culture.en: In the UK, 'Are you alright?' is often just a friendly hello, not a question about your health. 'Yes, thanks' or 'Fine, thanks' is enough.
culture.he: בבריטניה Are you alright? היא הרבה פעמים פשוט ברכה ידידותית, לא שאלה על מצבכם. מספיק לענות Yes, thanks או Fine, thanks.

culture.en: Clothing sizes use different numbers in the UK, the US and Europe, and they vary between brands. Check the label or ask.
culture.he: מידות בגדים מסומנות במספרים שונים בבריטניה, בארה״ב ובאירופה, וגם משתנות בין מותגים. כדאי לבדוק בתווית או לשאול.

variants.note: In the UK, 'pants' means underwear.
'Fitting room' works everywhere.
Where you pay. 'Checkout' works in both.
Spelling only.

scenarios.title_en: Returning an item: refund or store credit?
scenarios.title_he: החזרת מוצר: החזר כספי או זיכוי?

situation.en: Ten days ago you bought a pair of headphones at an electronics store in New York. The left side keeps cutting out. You have the box, but you can't find the paper receipt, only the payment in your banking app. (The store's policy in this scenario is invented for practice.)
situation.he: לפני עשרה ימים קניתם אוזניות בחנות אלקטרוניקה בניו יורק. הצליל באוזנייה השמאלית כל הזמן נקטע. הקופסה אצלכם, אבל את הקבלה המודפסת אתם לא מוצאים, יש רק את התשלום באפליקציה של הבנק. (מדיניות החנות בתרחיש הומצאה לצורך תרגול.)

goal.en: Explain the fault, offer proof of purchase, and politely but firmly push for a refund or a replacement instead of store credit.
goal.he: להסביר מה התקלה, להציג הוכחת קנייה, ולעמוד בנימוס ובתקיפות על החזר כספי או החלפה במקום זיכוי לחנות.

phrases.en: Hi, I'd like to return these, please.
phrases.he: שלום, הייתי רוצה להחזיר את אלה, בבקשה.

phrases.en: They stopped working after about a week.
phrases.he: הן הפסיקו לעבוד אחרי שבוע בערך.

phrases.en: The left side keeps cutting out.
phrases.he: הצליל באוזנייה השמאלית כל הזמן נקטע.
phrases.note: 'Cut out' = suddenly stop working, sometimes coming back on.

phrases.en: I can't find the receipt, but I paid by card. Here's the transaction in my banking app.
phrases.he: אני לא מוצא/ת את הקבלה, אבל שילמתי בכרטיס. הנה העסקה באפליקציה של הבנק.

phrases.en: Could I get a refund to my card?
If possible, I'd rather have a refund than store credit.
phrases.he: אם אפשר, אני מעדיף/ה החזר כספי ולא זיכוי.
phrases.note: 'Store credit' can only be spent in that shop.

phrases.en: Could I exchange them for a new pair instead?
Since they're defective, I'd expect a full refund.
phrases.he: מכיוון שהן פגומות, הייתי מצפה להחזר מלא.
phrases.note: Firm but not rude. 'Defective' (US) and 'faulty' (UK) both mean something is wrong with them, so they don't work properly.

phrases.en: I understand it's not your call. Is there anyone else I could talk to?
phrases.he: אני מבין/ה שזו לא ההחלטה שלך. יש מישהו אחר שאפשר לדבר איתו?
phrases.note: 'Not your call' = not your decision. A soft way to ask for someone more senior.

phrases.en: Could I speak to a manager, please?
phrases.note: Say it calmly, and only after you've tried to sort it out.

phrases.en: No worries, an exchange works for me.
Could I get a receipt for the return?

practice.partner: Hi there, what can I help you with today?

options.text: Your headphones are garbage. I want my money back.

feedback.en: Insulting the product (and the store) makes staff less willing to help. Stay polite and stick to the facts.
feedback.he: זלזול במוצר (ובחנות) רק מקטין את הרצון של הצוות לעזור לכם. עדיף להישאר מנומסים ועניינים.

options.text: Hi. I bought these here about ten days ago, and the left side keeps cutting out. I'd like to return them.

feedback.en: Clear and calm: what, when, the problem, and what you want.
feedback.he: ברור ורגוע: מה, מתי, מה הבעיה ומה אתם רוצים.

options.text: I want to return this. It's broken.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'I want' plus a short complaint sounds blunt. Describe the problem, then say 'I'd like to return them'.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל I want עם תלונה קצרה נשמע בוטה. עדיף לתאר את הבעיה ואז לומר I'd like to return them.

model_replies: Hi. I bought these here last week, and they've stopped working properly. I'd like to return them.
Hi, I'd like to return these headphones. The left side keeps cutting out.

practice.partner: Oh, sorry to hear that. Do you have your receipt?

options.text: No receipt. Card.

feedback.en: The idea is right, but it's too clipped. Full sentences make you sound calm and reasonable in a complaint.
feedback.he: הרעיון נכון, אבל קטוע מדי. בתלונה משפטים מלאים גורמים לכם להישמע רגועים והגיוניים.

options.text: I can't find it, unfortunately, but I paid by card. Here's the transaction.

feedback.en: You admit the problem and immediately offer other proof. 'Unfortunately' softens the bad news.
feedback.he: מודים בבעיה ומיד מציעים הוכחה אחרת. unfortunately מרכך את החדשות הפחות טובות.

options.text: No, but that's not my problem.

feedback.en: Sounds defensive and starts an argument. Offer another proof of purchase instead.
feedback.he: נשמע מתגונן ופותח ויכוח. עדיף להציע הוכחת קנייה אחרת.

model_replies: I can't find it, unfortunately, but I paid by card. Here's the transaction.
I'm afraid I've lost it, but I can show you the payment on my card.

practice.partner: OK. Without a receipt, the most I can do is store credit.

options.text: I see. The thing is, they're defective, so I'd really rather have a refund to my card.

feedback.en: 'I see' shows you listened; 'The thing is…' introduces your point without arguing; 'I'd rather' is firm but polite.
feedback.he: I see מראה שהקשבתם, The thing is... מציג את הטענה שלכם בלי להתווכח, ו-I'd rather תקיף אבל מנומס.

options.text: That's illegal. I'm going to call the police.

feedback.en: Threats escalate things fast, and you can't be sure what the law says. Ask politely, or ask for a manager.
feedback.he: איומים מסלימים את המצב מהר, ואתם גם לא בטוחים מה החוק אומר. עדיף לבקש בנימוס או לבקש מנהל.

options.text: No, I want a refund.

feedback.en: Clear, but blunt. You'll get further with 'I'd rather…' and a reason (they're defective).
feedback.he: ברור, אבל בוטה. תגיעו רחוק יותר עם I'd rather... ועם סיבה (they're defective).

model_replies: I see. The thing is, they're defective, so I'd really rather have a refund.
I understand, but since they're faulty, could I get a refund or a replacement instead?

practice.partner: I get that, but the system won't let me do a refund without a receipt.

options.text: Then I'd like to speak to your manager.

feedback.en: Reasonable, but jumping to the manager this early can feel like a threat. Suggest a solution first.
feedback.he: סביר, אבל לבקש מנהל כבר בשלב הזה עלול להרגיש כמו איום. כדאי קודם להציע פתרון.

options.text: The system is stupid. Just do it.

feedback.en: Rude, and the employee probably can't override the system. Offer an alternative instead.
feedback.he: גס, והעובד כנראה בכלל לא יכול לעקוף את המערכת. עדיף להציע חלופה.

options.text: Could you look up the purchase with my card? It was on the 14th.

feedback.en: A practical solution instead of repeating the complaint. Giving the date makes it easy for them.
feedback.he: פתרון מעשי במקום לחזור על התלונה. התאריך מקל על העובד למצוא את הקנייה.

model_replies: Could you look up the purchase with my card? It was on the 14th.
Is there any way to find the purchase on your system? I paid by card.

practice.partner: OK, found it. I can refund it to your card or swap them for a new pair. Which would you prefer?

options.text: Refund.

feedback.en: Clear, but abrupt after the employee went out of their way. Add 'please' or 'thanks'.
feedback.he: ברור, אבל חד מדי אחרי שהעובד התאמץ בשבילכם. כדאי להוסיף please או thanks.

options.text: A refund would be great. Thanks for looking it up.

feedback.en: A clear choice plus thanks for the extra effort. Ending on a positive note matters.
feedback.he: בחירה ברורה ותודה על המאמץ. חשוב לסיים בטון חיובי.

options.text: Finally. A refund, obviously.

feedback.en: Sarcastic and ungrateful. The employee just helped you; acknowledge it.
feedback.he: עוקצני וכפוי טובה. העובד הרגע עזר לכם, כדאי להכיר בזה.

model_replies: A refund would be great. Thanks for looking it up.
I'll take a new pair, thanks. I appreciate your help.

roleplay.persona: Tyler, a customer service associate at a large electronics store in New York. Friendly and laid-back, but nervous about breaking store rules.
roleplay.complication: With no paper receipt, Tyler first offers only store credit. He can find the purchase by card only if the learner suggests it and gives the date. If the learner stays polite, he offers a refund or a new pair; if the learner gets rude, he calls his manager, Denise, who is strict but fair and needs the whole story again.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey, how's it going? What can I help you with today?

culture.en: Return policies differ between stores and countries. Check the policy (often on the receipt or the store's website) and keep receipts until you're sure you're happy with a purchase.
culture.he: מדיניות ההחזרות משתנה בין חנויות ובין מדינות. כדאי לבדוק אותה (לרוב היא מופיעה על הקבלה או באתר החנות) ולשמור קבלות עד שבטוחים שהמוצר בסדר.

culture.en: A calm, polite complaint usually gets better results than an angry one. 'I understand, but…' and 'Is there anything you can do?' keep things friendly while you stand your ground.
culture.he: תלונה רגועה ומנומסת מביאה בדרך כלל תוצאות טובות יותר מתלונה כועסת. I understand, but... ו-Is there anything you can do? שומרים על אווירה נעימה בלי לוותר על העמדה שלכם.

culture.en: Asking for a manager is normal, but do it calmly and only after you've tried to sort things out with the first person.
culture.he: לבקש מנהל זה דבר מקובל, אבל עושים את זה ברוגע, ורק אחרי שניסיתם לפתור את העניין עם הנציג הראשון.

variants.note: Money you can only spend in that shop.
Both are understood everywhere.
British English uses 'store' for big shops, like a department store.

scenarios.title_en: Haggling at a market

situation.en: You're at a crafts market in Mexico City. You love a handwoven blanket, and you'd also like a couple of bracelets as gifts. Nothing has a price tag, and the seller expects some bargaining. (Prices in this scenario are made-up examples.)
situation.he: אתם בשוק אומנים במקסיקו סיטי. התאהבתם בשמיכה ארוגה ביד, ואתם רוצים גם כמה צמידים למתנה. אין תוויות מחיר, והמוכרת מצפה לקצת מיקוח. (המחירים בתרחיש הם דוגמה בלבד.)

goal.en: Ask the price, make a counter-offer and agree on a fair deal for several items, while keeping it friendly.
goal.he: לשאול כמה זה עולה, להציע מחיר נגדי ולהגיע לעסקה הוגנת על כמה פריטים, בלי לאבד את האווירה הנעימה.

phrases.en: How much is this one?
Is this handmade?
Is that your best price?
phrases.note: The most common friendly way to start bargaining.

phrases.en: It's beautiful, but it's a bit more than I wanted to spend.
phrases.he: זה יפהפה, אבל זה קצת יותר ממה שתכננתי להוציא.

phrases.en: Would you take 600?
phrases.note: 'Would you take…?' = would you accept this price?

phrases.en: What if I buy two? Could you do a better price?
phrases.he: ואם אקנה שניים? אפשר מחיר יותר טוב?

phrases.en: Could you do all three for 900?
phrases.note: 'Do' here means 'sell for': 'Can you do it for 500?'

phrases.en: Meet me in the middle?
phrases.note: = Let's both move a little and agree on a price in between. 'Meet me halfway?' is also common.

phrases.en: Do you give a discount for cash?
Thanks anyway, I'll think about it.
phrases.he: תודה בכל מקרה, אני אחשוב על זה.
phrases.note: A polite way to walk away. Sometimes the seller calls you back with a better offer.

phrases.en: OK, it's a deal!

practice.partner: Hello! Come and have a look. Everything is handmade.

options.text: How much is cost this?

feedback.en: Two structures mixed together. Say 'How much is this?' or 'How much does this cost?'
feedback.he: ערבוב של שני מבנים. אומרים How much is this? או How much does this cost?

options.text: How much?

feedback.en: Common at markets and understood, but a little cold. A 'thanks' or a compliment helps when you plan to bargain.
feedback.he: נפוץ בשווקים ומובן, אבל קצת קר. כשמתכננים להתמקח, תודה או מחמאה עוזרות.

options.text: Thanks. This blanket is beautiful. How much is it?

feedback.en: A compliment first creates goodwill, then a simple question.
feedback.he: מחמאה בהתחלה יוצרת אווירה טובה, ואחריה שאלה פשוטה.

model_replies: Thanks. This blanket is beautiful. How much is it?
Wow, these are lovely. How much is this one?

practice.partner: That one is 900 pesos. It took my sister two weeks to make.

options.text: It's lovely, but that's a bit more than I wanted to spend. Would you take 600?

feedback.en: Compliment, gentle reason, clear offer: the classic friendly way to bargain.
feedback.he: מחמאה, סיבה עדינה והצעה ברורה: הדרך הקלאסית להתמקח בנעימות.

options.text: Too expensive. 600.

feedback.en: Clear, but blunt. Sellers respond better to 'That's a bit much for me. Would you take 600?'
feedback.he: ברור, אבל בוטה. מוכרים מגיבים טוב יותר ל-That's a bit much for me. Would you take 600?

options.text: 900? Are you crazy? That's a tourist price.

feedback.en: Insulting the seller is the fastest way to end the bargaining. Show interest, then make an offer.
feedback.he: להעליב את המוכרת זו הדרך המהירה ביותר לסיים את המיקוח. עדיף להראות עניין ואז להציע מחיר.

model_replies: It's lovely, but that's a bit more than I wanted to spend. Would you take 600?
Hmm, is that your best price? How about 650?

practice.partner: 600? No, no, it's real wool. I can do 850.

options.text: No. 600 or I go.

feedback.en: An ultimatum sounds aggressive. If you want to walk away, do it politely: 'Thanks anyway, I'll think about it.'
feedback.he: אולטימטום נשמע תוקפני. אם רוצים לוותר, עושים את זה בנימוס: Thanks anyway, I'll think about it.

options.text: What if I take two of these bracelets as well? Could you do all three for 900?

feedback.en: Buying more gives the seller a reason to lower the price. 'What if…' and 'Could you do…' keep it friendly.
feedback.he: קנייה של יותר פריטים נותנת למוכרת סיבה להוריד מחיר. What if... ו-Could you do... שומרים על טון ידידותי.

options.text: 850 is still too much. 700.

feedback.en: Acceptable at a market, but you're only pushing the number. Offering to buy more works better.
feedback.he: מקובל בשוק, אבל אתם רק לוחצים על המספר. הצעה לקנות עוד פריטים עובדת טוב יותר.

model_replies: What if I take two bracelets as well? Could you do all three for 900?
OK, and if I buy these bracelets too, can you do a better price?

practice.partner: All three? 1,000, and that's a very good price.

options.text: Hmm, I'm not sure. It's still a little out of my budget.

feedback.en: Polite, but it doesn't move the deal forward. Add a number so the seller knows what you'd accept.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל לא מקדם את העסקה. כדאי להוסיף מספר כדי שהמוכרת תדע על מה תסכימו.

options.text: You're lying, that's not a good price.

feedback.en: Calling someone a liar is very offensive. Disagree with the price, not the person.
feedback.he: לקרוא למישהו שקרן זה מעליב מאוד. מתווכחים על המחיר, לא על האדם.

options.text: Meet me in the middle? 950, and I'll pay cash.

feedback.en: A friendly compromise, and cash is often a good argument at a market.
feedback.he: פשרה ידידותית, ומזומן הוא לרוב טיעון טוב בשוק.

model_replies: Meet me in the middle? 950, and I'll pay cash.
How about 950 if I pay cash?

practice.partner: OK, OK, 950. You drive a hard bargain!

options.text: Thank you! It's a deal. They'll make great gifts.

feedback.en: Warm and gracious. Once you agree, accept happily and stop pushing.
feedback.he: חם ואדיב. אחרי שמסכימים על מחיר, מקבלים אותו בשמחה ומפסיקים ללחוץ.

options.text: What about 900?

feedback.en: Trying to go lower after the seller has agreed is bad manners. A deal is a deal.
feedback.he: לנסות להוריד שוב אחרי שהמוכרת הסכימה זה חוסר נימוס. מה שסוכם, סוכם.

options.text: OK, deal.

feedback.en: Fine, but a 'thank you' after friendly bargaining leaves a better feeling.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל תודה בסוף מיקוח ידידותי משאירה טעם טוב יותר.

model_replies: Thank you! It's a deal.
Great, deal! Thanks so much.

roleplay.persona: Lupita, a weaver who sells her family's blankets and bracelets at a crafts market in Mexico City. Warm, funny and proud of her work; she enjoys a good bargain but won't sell below a fair price.
roleplay.complication: Lupita starts high and won't go below 850 for the blanket alone. She only gives a real discount if the learner buys more than one item or pays cash. If the learner is rude about the price, she stops negotiating; if the learner politely walks away, she calls them back with one last offer.
roleplay.opening_line: Hola! Hello! Come and have a look. Everything here is made by my family.

culture.en: In many markets around the world, bargaining is normal and even expected, but it should feel friendly, like a game. In shops with price tags, especially in the UK and the US, people usually don't bargain.
culture.he: בשווקים רבים בעולם מיקוח הוא דבר רגיל ואפילו צפוי, אבל הוא אמור להרגיש ידידותי, כמו משחק. בחנויות עם תוויות מחיר, בעיקר בבריטניה ובארה״ב, בדרך כלל לא מתמקחים.

culture.en: Israeli-style directness ('Too expensive! 500, final!') can sound aggressive in English. Soften your offers: 'Would you take…?', 'Is that your best price?'
culture.he: הישירות הישראלית ('יקר! 500 וזהו!') עלולה להישמע תוקפנית באנגלית. כדאי לרכך: Would you take...? או Is that your best price?

culture.en: Only offer a price you're really willing to pay. If the seller accepts, backing out is rude.
culture.he: מציעים רק מחיר שבאמת מוכנים לשלם. אם המוכר מסכים, לחזור בכם מההצעה זה לא מנומס.

scenarios.title_en: At the checkout: card declined

situation.en: You're paying for a few books at a bookstore in Chicago. You'd like to know if there's a student discount. Then you tap your card, and the payment doesn't go through. (Prices and discounts in this scenario are made-up examples.)
situation.he: אתם משלמים על כמה ספרים בחנות ספרים בשיקגו ורוצים לדעת אם יש הנחת סטודנטים. אחר כך אתם מצמידים את הכרטיס, והתשלום לא עובר. (המחירים וההנחות בתרחיש הם דוגמה בלבד.)

goal.en: Ask about a discount, stay calm when your card is declined, find another way to pay and get your receipt.
goal.he: לשאול על הנחה, להישאר רגועים כשהכרטיס נדחה, למצוא דרך אחרת לשלם ולקבל קבלה.

phrases.en: Do you have a student discount?
Is this on sale?
phrases.note: In the US, 'on sale' means the price is reduced.

phrases.en: Is this in the sale?
phrases.note: In the UK, 'on sale' can just mean 'available to buy'; 'in the sale' means reduced.

phrases.en: Sorry, could you try it one more time?
That's weird. It worked this morning.
Can I try a different card?
I'll pay in cash, then.
Sorry, I'm holding up the line.
Sorry, I'm holding up the queue.
Could I get a receipt, please?
Could you email it to me instead?
phrases.he: אפשר לשלוח לי אותה במייל במקום?

phrases.en: No bag, thanks.
