model_dialogue.text: Could you email it to me instead? And no bag, thanks.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure, just type your email here. Have a good one!

practice.partner: Hi there. Did you find everything OK?

options.text: Why do you ask me this?

feedback.en: It's just a routine, friendly question, not a real request for information. A suspicious answer sounds strange.
feedback.he: זו שאלת נימוס שגרתית, לא באמת בקשת מידע. תשובה חשדנית נשמעת מוזרה.

options.text: Yes, thanks. Do you have a student discount, by the way?

feedback.en: A quick, friendly answer, then your question. 'By the way' makes it sound relaxed.
feedback.he: תשובה קצרה ונעימה, ואחריה השאלה שלכם. by the way נותן לזה טון רגוע.

options.text: Yes.

feedback.en: Fine, but it can sound cold. 'Yes, thanks' is the usual answer.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל עלול להישמע קר. התשובה הרגילה היא Yes, thanks.

model_replies: Yes, thanks. Do you have a student discount, by the way?
Yes, thank you. Is there a student discount?

practice.partner: We do, ten percent with a student ID. Do you have one with you?

options.text: Yes, I have it. Here is my student identity card.

feedback.en: Correct, but formal. People just say 'student ID' (US) or 'student card' (UK).
feedback.he: נכון, אבל רשמי. אומרים פשוט student ID (ארה״ב) או student card (בריטניה).

options.text: Yes, here you go.

feedback.en: Natural and quick: the cashier can see what you're handing over.
feedback.he: טבעי ומהיר: הקופאי רואה מה אתם מגישים.

options.text: No, but I am student, believe me.

feedback.en: Missing 'a' ('I'm a student'), and asking them to just believe you puts the cashier in an awkward position.
feedback.he: חסר a (I'm a student), ולבקש מהקופאי פשוט להאמין לכם מעמיד אותו במצב לא נעים.

model_replies: Yes, here you go.
Yep, here it is.

practice.partner: Hmm, it says declined. Do you want to try again?

options.text: Your machine is broken.

feedback.en: Blaming their card machine sounds rude, and the problem is often with your bank. Try again or use another card.
feedback.he: להאשים את מכשיר התשלום של החנות נשמע גס, והבעיה היא לעיתים קרובות בבנק שלכם. נסו שוב או השתמשו בכרטיס אחר.

options.text: Yes, again.

feedback.en: Understandable, but abrupt. 'Sure, let me try again' sounds friendlier.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל חד. Sure, let me try again נשמע נעים יותר.

options.text: That's weird, it worked this morning. Can I insert it instead?

feedback.en: You stay calm, don't blame anyone ('That's weird…') and suggest a solution.
feedback.he: נשארים רגועים, לא מאשימים אף אחד (That's weird...) ומציעים פתרון.

model_replies: That's weird, it worked this morning. Can I insert it instead?
Sure, let me try again.

practice.partner: No, sorry, still declined.

options.text: Sorry about this. I'll pay in cash, then.

feedback.en: A short apology for the delay plus a quick solution. Very natural.
feedback.he: התנצלות קצרה על העיכוב ופתרון מהיר. טבעי מאוד.

options.text: What I do now?

feedback.en: Questions need a helping verb: 'What should I do now?' Better still, suggest another way to pay.
feedback.he: בשאלה צריך פועל עזר: What should I do now? ועוד יותר טוב להציע דרך תשלום אחרת.

options.text: I have cash. I will pay with the cash.

feedback.en: Understandable, but stiff, and 'the cash' sounds odd. 'I'll pay in cash, then' is shorter and more natural.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל נוקשה, ו-the cash נשמע מוזר. I'll pay in cash, then קצר וטבעי יותר.

model_replies: Sorry about this. I'll pay in cash, then.
Sorry! Can I try a different card?

practice.partner: Here's your change. Do you want the receipt in the bag?

options.text: No bag. Email.

feedback.en: Understandable, but too clipped. Make it a request: 'Could you email it to me?'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל קטוע מדי. עדיף לנסח כבקשה: Could you email it to me?

options.text: Could you email it to me instead? And no bag, thanks.

feedback.en: Polite request plus a quick 'no bag, thanks'. Exactly how people say it.
feedback.he: בקשה מנומסת ו-no bag, thanks קצר. בדיוק כמו שאומרים את זה.

options.text: I don't need. Give me the check.

feedback.en: 'Check' is the bill at a restaurant (US), not a receipt, and 'I don't need' needs an object: 'I don't need one'.
feedback.he: check זה החשבון במסעדה (בארה״ב), לא קבלה. וגם אחרי I don't need צריך מושא: I don't need one.

model_replies: Could you email it to me instead? And no bag, thanks.
In the bag is fine, thanks.

roleplay.persona: Marcus, a cashier at a busy bookstore in Chicago. Easygoing and patient, he likes chatting about the books people buy, but there's a long line behind the learner.
roleplay.complication: The learner's card is declined twice, and the store's card reader won't accept the learner's second idea, so they need another solution (cash, another card, or putting a book back). The student discount only applies with a valid student ID, and Marcus asks to see it.
roleplay.opening_line: Hi there! Did you find everything OK today?

culture.en: In most US states, the price on the shelf doesn't include sales tax. It's added at the register, so the total is often a little higher than you expect.
culture.he: ברוב מדינות ארה״ב המחיר על המדף לא כולל מס מכירה. המס מתווסף בקופה, ולכן הסכום הסופי לרוב קצת גבוה ממה שציפיתם.

culture.en: If your card is declined abroad, your bank may have blocked the payment as a security check. Check your banking app or call the bank, and carry a backup way to pay.
culture.he: אם הכרטיס נדחה בחו״ל, ייתכן שהבנק חסם את העסקה כבדיקת אבטחה. כדאי לבדוק באפליקציה של הבנק או להתקשר אליו, ותמיד להחזיק אמצעי תשלום נוסף.

culture.en: Cashiers often ask 'Did you find everything OK?' or 'How's your day going?' A short, friendly answer is all they expect.
culture.he: קופאים שואלים הרבה פעמים Did you find everything OK? או How's your day going? מצפים רק לתשובה קצרה ונעימה.

variants.note: 'Checkout' works in both.
Both mean the price is reduced.

scenarios.title_en: Meeting travellers in a hostel

situation.en: You've just arrived at a hostel in Chiang Mai, Thailand. In the common room, a traveller is looking at a map, planning what to do tomorrow. She looks friendly.
situation.he: הגעתם עכשיו להוסטל בצ'יאנג מאי שבתאילנד. בחדר המשותף יושבת מטיילת, מסתכלת על מפה ומתכננת מה לעשות מחר. היא נראית ידידותית.

goal.en: Introduce yourself, talk about your travel plans, and make a plan to do something together tomorrow.
goal.he: להציג את עצמכם, לדבר על תוכניות הטיול שלכם ולקבוע לעשות משהו ביחד מחר.

phrases.en: Hey, mind if I join you?
phrases.note: Very common in hostels. 'Do you mind if I sit here?' is a little more polite. The friendly answer is 'Not at all' or 'Go ahead' (= I don't mind).

phrases.en: Hi, I'm Tal. I just got in today.
phrases.note: 'Get in' = arrive (at a place you're staying).

phrases.en: Where are you from?
How long have you been travelling?
phrases.note: Present perfect continuous: an activity that started in the past and is still going on.

phrases.en: Where are you headed next?
I'm here for about a week, then I'm heading south to the islands.
phrases.he: אני פה בערך שבוע, ואז אני ממשיך/ה דרומה לאיים.

phrases.en: Have you been anywhere good so far?
Any tips for Chiang Mai?
Would you mind if I came along?
phrases.note: 'Come along' = join you. After 'Would you mind if…', use the past simple.

phrases.en: That sounds great, count me in!
What time are you leaving?
Want to swap numbers?
phrases.note: Or: 'Are you on WhatsApp?'

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hi! Are you new? I haven't seen you around.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yeah, I just got in this afternoon. I'm Tal, from Israel. Mind if I join you?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Not at all, have a seat! I'm Lena, from Hamburg.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Nice to meet you. How long have you been travelling?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: About two months now. I started in Vietnam. What about you?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Only a week. I'm here for a few days, then I'm heading south to the islands.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Nice. Tomorrow a few of us are doing a cooking class. You should come!

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Oh, I'd love to! What time does it start?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: They pick us up here at nine. I can ask if there's still space.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Amazing, thanks. Want to swap numbers so you can let me know?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure! Here, put your number in my phone.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: There you go. See you at nine, then!

practice.partner: Hi! Are you new? I haven't seen you around.

options.text: Yes. My name is Tal. I am from Israel.

feedback.en: Correct, but it sounds like a textbook. In a hostel, people say 'I'm Tal' and use short forms.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל נשמע כמו ספר לימוד. בהוסטל אומרים I'm Tal ומשתמשים בצורות מקוצרות.

options.text: Yeah, I just got in this afternoon. I'm Tal, from Israel.

feedback.en: Relaxed and friendly: you answer and introduce yourself in one go.
feedback.he: רגוע וידידותי: עונים ומציגים את עצמכם באותה נשימה.

options.text: Yes, I came now.

feedback.en: 'I came now' is a word-for-word translation from Hebrew. Say 'I just got here' or 'I just arrived'.
feedback.he: I came now זה תרגום מילה במילה של 'הגעתי עכשיו'. באנגלית אומרים I just got here או I just arrived.

model_replies: Yeah, I just got in this afternoon. I'm Tal, from Israel.
Yes, I just arrived today. I'm Tal. Nice to meet you!

practice.partner: I'm Lena, from Hamburg. So how long are you in Thailand for?

options.text: I am in Thailand since one week.

feedback.en: This follows Hebrew grammar. English uses the present perfect with 'for': 'I've been in Thailand for a week.'
feedback.he: זה מבנה מהעברית. באנגלית משתמשים ב-present perfect עם for: I've been in Thailand for a week.

options.text: Three weeks.

feedback.en: Correct, but very short. Add a detail and ask her back to keep the conversation going.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל קצר מאוד. כדאי להוסיף פרט ולשאול אותה בחזרה כדי שהשיחה תימשך.

options.text: About three weeks. I'm here for a few days, then I'm heading south. What about you?

feedback.en: A clear plan, natural travel language ('heading south'), and a question back.
feedback.he: תוכנית ברורה, שפת טיולים טבעית (heading south) ושאלה בחזרה.

model_replies: About three weeks. I'm here for a few days, then I'm heading south.
Three weeks in total. I've been here for a week so far. How about you?

practice.partner: I started in Vietnam two months ago. It was amazing.

options.text: Two months, wow! What was your favourite place?

feedback.en: You show interest and ask a follow-up question, which keeps the conversation going.
feedback.he: מראים עניין ושואלים שאלת המשך, וכך השיחה ממשיכה לזרום.

options.text: Nice.

feedback.en: Friendly, but it closes the topic. Add a question like 'What was the best part?'
feedback.he: ידידותי, אבל סוגר את הנושא. כדאי להוסיף שאלה כמו What was the best part?

options.text: I don't like Vietnam.

feedback.en: Negative and a bit rude when she's sharing something she loved. Show interest first.
feedback.he: שלילי וקצת לא נעים כשהיא משתפת במשהו שאהבה. קודם מראים עניין.

model_replies: Two months, wow! What was your favourite place?
That's so cool. What was the best part?

practice.partner: Tomorrow a few of us are doing a cooking class. You should come!

options.text: OK, I will come.

feedback.en: Correct, but flat. Show some enthusiasm: 'I'd love to!' or 'Count me in!'
feedback.he: נכון, אבל יבש. כדאי להראות התלהבות: I'd love to! או Count me in!

options.text: Maybe. How much it costs?

feedback.en: Asking the price is fine, but the question needs 'does': 'How much does it cost?' Show a bit of interest first.
feedback.he: לגיטימי לשאול על המחיר, אבל בשאלה צריך does: How much does it cost? וכדאי קודם להראות קצת עניין.

options.text: Oh, I'd love to! What time does it start?

feedback.en: Warm acceptance plus a practical question.
feedback.he: הסכמה חמה ושאלה מעשית.

model_replies: Oh, I'd love to! What time does it start?
Count me in! How much is it?

practice.partner: They pick us up here at nine. I can ask if there's still space.

options.text: Amazing, thanks! Want to swap numbers so you can let me know?

feedback.en: Natural and practical: you give a reason for asking for her number.
feedback.he: טבעי ומעשי: נותנים סיבה לבקשת המספר.

options.text: OK, bye.

feedback.en: Ends things too suddenly, and you'll have no way to find out if there's space.
feedback.he: מסיים בפתאומיות, ואין לכם דרך לדעת אם נשאר מקום.

options.text: Thank you. Give me your phone number.

feedback.en: Clear, but 'Give me' sounds like an order. Ask: 'Want to swap numbers?' or 'Can I get your number?'
feedback.he: ברור, אבל Give me נשמע כמו פקודה. עדיף לשאול: Want to swap numbers? או Can I get your number?

model_replies: Amazing, thanks! Want to swap numbers so you can let me know?
Great, thanks. Are you on WhatsApp?

roleplay.persona: Lena, 24, a traveller from Hamburg on a gap year. Talkative and curious, she's been on the road for two months and loves giving tips.
roleplay.complication: The cooking class turns out to be full. Lena suggests an alternative: an early hike to a waterfall that leaves at 6:30. The learner has to agree on a plan, a time and a meeting place, and swap contacts.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey! Are you new here? I haven't seen you around before.

culture.en: In hostels it's normal to talk to strangers and join their plans. 'Mind if I join you?' is all you need to start.
culture.he: בהוסטלים מקובל לדבר עם זרים ולהצטרף לתוכניות שלהם. Mind if I join you? זה כל מה שצריך כדי להתחיל.

culture.en: Travellers often ask 'Where are you from?', 'How long are you travelling for?' and 'Where are you headed next?' Have a short answer ready, and ask the same question back.
culture.he: מטיילים שואלים הרבה Where are you from?, How long are you travelling for? ו-Where are you headed next? כדאי שתהיה לכם תשובה קצרה מוכנה, ולשאול את אותה שאלה בחזרה.

culture.en: Meeting people on the road is part of the fun, but keep basic safety in mind: meet in public places and tell someone you trust about your plans.
culture.he: היכרויות בדרך הן חלק מהכיף, אבל כדאי לשמור על כללי בטיחות בסיסיים: להיפגש במקומות ציבוריים ולספר למישהו שאתם סומכים עליו על התוכניות שלכם.

variants.note: Spelling only.
Spelling only.
Backpackers on a long trip usually just say 'my trip'.

scenarios.title_en: Small talk at a party

situation.en: You're at a friend's birthday party in London. You only know the host, Sam. A woman is standing near you by the snacks, and you'd like to start a conversation.
situation.he: אתם במסיבת יום הולדת של חבר בלונדון, ומכירים רק את המארח, סאם. לצדכם, ליד שולחן החטיפים, עומדת בחורה, ואתם רוצים לפתוח איתה בשיחה.

goal.en: Start a conversation, keep it going with follow-up questions, and end it politely.
goal.he: לפתוח בשיחה, להמשיך אותה עם שאלות המשך ולסיים אותה בנימוס.

phrases.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Tal.
phrases.he: היי, נראה לי שעוד לא הכרנו. אני טל.

phrases.en: So, how do you know Sam?
phrases.he: אז מאיפה את/ה מכיר/ה את סאם?
phrases.note: The classic opener at a party: everyone there knows the host.

phrases.en: Have you tried these? They're really good.
phrases.he: טעמת את אלה? הם ממש טובים.

phrases.en: Oh really? How did you get into that?
phrases.note: 'Get into' = start doing or liking something.

phrases.en: That sounds amazing. What's it like?
What do you like doing when you're not working?
phrases.he: מה את/ה אוהב/ת לעשות כשאת/ה לא בעבודה?
phrases.note: Friendlier than only asking about someone's job.

phrases.en: Same here!
phrases.note: Shows you have something in common.

phrases.en: No way! I've always wanted to go there.
phrases.he: מה, באמת? תמיד רציתי להגיע לשם.
phrases.note: 'No way!' here shows surprise, not disagreement.

phrases.en: Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
phrases.he: סליחה, לא קלטתי איך קוראים לך.
phrases.note: 'Catch' = hear or understand.

phrases.en: Anyway, I'm going to get a drink. It was really nice talking to you.
phrases.he: טוב, אני הולך/ת להביא משהו לשתות. היה ממש נחמד לדבר איתך.
phrases.note: A natural way to end a conversation at a party.

phrases.en: I'll let you get back to your friends.
phrases.he: לא אעכב אותך, תחזור/י לחברים שלך.
phrases.note: A kind way to end a chat without sounding bored.

phrases.en: Great to meet you. Enjoy the rest of the party!

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Tal.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Oh, hi! I'm Jess. Nice to meet you.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: You too. So, how do you know Sam?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: We work together at a design studio. What about you?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: We're on the same course at uni. I'm here on an exchange year from Israel.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Oh, cool! How are you finding London?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I love it, apart from the weather! What kind of design do you do?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Mostly book covers. It's fun, but the deadlines are crazy.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Oh wow, that sounds amazing! How did you get into that?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: I was always drawing as a kid, and it just sort of happened. Do you draw at all?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Not really, I'm more into photography. I'd love to see some of your covers, though!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure! I'll show you some on my phone later.

practice.partner: Oh, hi! I'm Jess. So, how do you know Sam?

options.text: From university.

feedback.en: Correct, but it gives Jess nothing to continue with. Add a detail or ask her back.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל לא נותן לג'ס במה להמשיך. כדאי להוסיף פרט או לשאול אותה בחזרה.

options.text: Why do you want to know?

feedback.en: Sounds defensive. At a party, this question is just a friendly way to start talking.
feedback.he: נשמע מתגונן. במסיבה זו פשוט דרך ידידותית להתחיל לדבר.

options.text: We're on the same course at uni. What about you?

feedback.en: Answer briefly, then ask the same question back: that's the key to small talk.
feedback.he: עונים בקצרה ושואלים את אותה שאלה בחזרה: זה הסוד של שיחת חולין.

model_replies: We're on the same course at uni. What about you?
We study together. How about you? How do you know him?

practice.partner: Oh, cool! How are you finding London?

options.text: I love it, apart from the weather! How long have you lived here?

feedback.en: A real answer with a light joke, then a question back.
feedback.he: תשובה אמיתית עם קצת הומור, ואחריה שאלה בחזרה.

options.text: I found it on Google Maps.

feedback.en: A misunderstanding: 'How are you finding London?' means 'Do you like it? How is it for you?'
feedback.he: אי-הבנה: How are you finding London? פירושו 'מה דעתך על לונדון?', ולא איך מצאת אותה.

options.text: It is good.

feedback.en: Correct but flat. Add a detail ('apart from the weather', 'the parks are amazing') and a question.
feedback.he: נכון אבל יבש. כדאי להוסיף פרט (apart from the weather או the parks are amazing) ושאלה.

model_replies: I love it, apart from the weather! How long have you lived here?
It's amazing, but really expensive! Are you from London?

practice.partner: I design book covers, mostly. It's fun, but the deadlines are crazy.

options.text: How much money do you make?

feedback.en: Too personal. In most English-speaking cultures, you don't ask about salary when you've just met someone.
feedback.he: אישי מדי. ברוב התרבויות דוברות האנגלית לא שואלים על משכורת מישהו שרק הכרתם.

options.text: Oh wow, that sounds amazing! How did you get into that?

feedback.en: Enthusiasm plus an open question ('How…?') invites a longer answer.
feedback.he: התלהבות ושאלה פתוחה (How...?) מזמינות תשובה ארוכה יותר.

options.text: Do you like your job?

feedback.en: A yes/no question, and she's already told you it's fun. Open questions ('How did you…?', 'What's it like…?') work better.
feedback.he: שאלת כן/לא, והיא כבר אמרה שזה כיף. שאלות פתוחות (How did you...?, What's it like...?) עובדות טוב יותר.

model_replies: Oh wow, that sounds amazing! How did you get into that?
That sounds so interesting. What's the best cover you've done?

practice.partner: I was always drawing as a kid, and it just sort of happened. Do you draw at all?

options.text: No.

feedback.en: Honest, but it stops the conversation. Say what you do instead: 'Not really, I'm more into…'
feedback.he: כנה, אבל עוצר את השיחה. כדאי לספר מה כן: Not really, I'm more into...

options.text: Not really, I'm more into photography. I'd love to see some of your covers, though!

feedback.en: You share something about yourself and show interest in her work.
feedback.he: משתפים משהו על עצמכם ומראים עניין בעבודה שלה.

options.text: No, drawing is for children.

feedback.en: Rude, especially to someone who draws for a living.
feedback.he: גס, במיוחד כלפי מישהי שמתפרנסת מאיור.

model_replies: Not really, I'm more into photography. I'd love to see some of your covers, though!
Not at all, but I love art. Do you have any of your work on your phone?

practice.partner: Anyway, I should go and say hi to Sam's sister. She's just arrived.

options.text: Wait, you didn't tell me how old you are.

feedback.en: Holding someone back with a personal question is awkward. Let her go with a friendly line.
feedback.he: לעכב מישהו עם שאלה אישית זה מביך. עדיף לשחרר אותה במשפט נעים.

options.text: OK. Goodbye, Jess.

feedback.en: Polite, but 'Goodbye' sounds final and formal at a party. 'See you later!' is warmer.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל Goodbye נשמע סופי ורשמי במסיבה. See you later! חם יותר.

options.text: Of course! It was really nice talking to you. See you later!

feedback.en: Warm and natural, and it leaves the door open to talk again.
feedback.he: חם וטבעי, ומשאיר פתח לדבר שוב.

model_replies: Of course! It was really nice talking to you. See you later!
Sure, go ahead! Great to meet you, Jess.

roleplay.persona: Jess, 27, a graphic designer and a colleague of the host. Friendly but a little shy at first; she opens up when people ask real questions about her work and her travels.
roleplay.complication: Jess gives short answers at first, so the learner has to ask open follow-up questions to keep the conversation alive. Later the music gets loud and she mishears something, so the learner has to repeat or rephrase. Finally, the learner should end the chat politely.
roleplay.opening_line: Oh, hi! Are you a friend of Sam's too?

culture.en: Safe small-talk topics: how you know the host, work or studies, travel, food, films and the weather. With someone you've just met, avoid salary, religion and politics.
culture.he: נושאים בטוחים לשיחת חולין: איך מכירים את המארח, עבודה או לימודים, טיולים, אוכל, סרטים ומזג האוויר. עם מישהו שרק הכרתם עדיף להימנע משכר, דת ופוליטיקה.

culture.en: Small talk is like ping-pong: answer, add a detail, then ask something back. One-word answers can seem unfriendly in English.
culture.he: שיחת חולין היא כמו פינג-פונג: עונים, מוסיפים פרט ושואלים משהו בחזרה. באנגלית תשובות של מילה אחת עלולות להיראות לא ידידותיות.

culture.en: At parties, people move on after a few minutes. 'Anyway, it was great talking to you' is a polite way to end a chat; nobody will be offended.
culture.he: במסיבות נהוג לעבור בין אנשים אחרי כמה דקות. Anyway, it was great talking to you היא דרך מנומסת לסיים שיחה, ואף אחד לא ייעלב.

variants.note: Americans often say 'college' even for a university.
'What are you studying?' works everywhere.

scenarios.title_en: Invitations: accepting, declining and rescheduling

situation.en: You're spending a semester in Boston. Your classmate Chris calls to invite you to the movies with some friends on Friday night, but you already have plans that evening.
situation.he: אתם בסמסטר לימודים בבוסטון. חבר לכיתה, כריס, מתקשר להזמין אתכם לסרט עם כמה חברים ביום שישי בערב, אבל באותו ערב כבר יש לכם תוכניות.

goal.en: Decline politely with a reason, suggest another day, agree on the details, and reschedule smoothly if plans change.
goal.he: לסרב בנימוס עם סיבה, להציע יום אחר, לסגור את הפרטים, ולדחות בצורה נעימה אם התוכניות משתנות.

phrases.en: Are you free on Saturday?
Would you like to come to the movies with us?
Do you fancy coming to the cinema with us?
phrases.note: 'Do you fancy…?' is very British.

phrases.en: I'd love to, but I can't make it on Friday.
phrases.he: הייתי שמח/ה, אבל ביום שישי אני לא יכול/ה.
phrases.note: 'Make it' = manage to come.

phrases.en: I've already got plans, unfortunately.
How about Saturday instead?
Sounds good! What time works for you?
phrases.he: נשמע טוב! איזו שעה מתאימה לך?

phrases.en: Count me in!
Something's come up. Could we do another day?
phrases.he: צץ לי משהו. אפשר לעשות את זה ביום אחר?
phrases.note: 'Something's come up' = something unexpected has happened. You don't have to explain more.

phrases.en: Can I take a rain check?
phrases.note: = Not this time, but I'd like to another time. Mainly American, but widely understood.

phrases.en: Sorry for the short notice.
Thanks so much for the invite!
phrases.note: 'Invite' as a noun is informal; write 'invitation' in formal messages.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hey! What are you up to on Friday night?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hey, Chris! Why, what's up?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: A few of us are going to the movies, and then getting pizza. Want to come?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Oh, I'd love to, but I can't make it on Friday. I've already got plans with my roommates.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Aw, that's too bad. What about Saturday? We could do the movie then.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Saturday works! What time were you thinking?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Maybe the seven o'clock show, then pizza after?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sounds perfect, count me in. Where should we meet?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Let's meet outside the theater at a quarter to seven.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great. Thanks so much for the invite!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course! Oh, and Maya might come too.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Even better. See you Saturday!

practice.partner: Hey! A few of us are going to the movies on Friday night. Want to come?

options.text: No, I can't. I'm busy.

feedback.en: Honest, but it sounds cold, as if you're not interested. Start with 'I'd love to, but…'
feedback.he: כנה, אבל נשמע קר, כאילו זה לא מעניין אתכם. כדאי להתחיל ב-I'd love to, but...

options.text: Oh, I'd love to, but I can't make it on Friday. I've already got plans.

feedback.en: Warm first ('I'd love to'), then a soft no with a short reason. Very natural.
feedback.he: קודם חום (I'd love to), ואחר כך סירוב רך עם סיבה קצרה. טבעי מאוד.

options.text: No, I don't want to go with you.

feedback.en: Very hurtful, even if you're just busy. If you're not interested, use a soft line: 'Thanks, but I'll pass this time.'
feedback.he: פוגע מאוד, גם אם אתם פשוט עסוקים. אם זה לא מעניין אתכם, אפשר לסרב ברכות: Thanks, but I'll pass this time.

model_replies: Oh, I'd love to, but I can't make it on Friday. I've already got plans.
Thanks for asking! Friday's tricky for me, though. Could we do another day?

practice.partner: Aw, that's too bad. What about Saturday instead?

options.text: Saturday I can. When it starts?

feedback.en: Word order: 'I can do Saturday', and the question needs 'does': 'When does it start?'
feedback.he: סדר מילים: I can do Saturday, ובשאלה צריך does: When does it start?

options.text: Saturday works! What time were you thinking?

feedback.en: Enthusiastic and moves the plan forward. 'What time were you thinking?' is a soft way to ask.
feedback.he: נלהב ומקדם את התוכנית. What time were you thinking? היא דרך רכה לשאול.

options.text: Yes, Saturday is possible.

feedback.en: Correct, but formal and a bit flat. 'Saturday works!' or 'Saturday's great!' sounds keener.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל רשמי וקצת יבש. Saturday works! או Saturday's great! נשמעים נלהבים יותר.

model_replies: Saturday works! What time were you thinking?
Saturday's great. What time?

practice.partner: Maybe the seven o'clock show, then pizza after?

options.text: Sounds perfect, count me in! Where should we meet?

feedback.en: Clear yes, some enthusiasm, and a practical next step.
feedback.he: 'כן' ברור, קצת התלהבות וצעד מעשי להמשך.

options.text: I will think and I will tell you.

feedback.en: Sounds unsure after you've just said Saturday works, and it's translated word for word from Hebrew. The natural phrase is 'Let me think about it and get back to you', but here it's better to just say yes.
feedback.he: נשמע מהסס אחרי שרק עכשיו אמרתם ששבת מתאימה, וזה תרגום מילולי של 'אחשוב ואגיד לך'. הניסוח הטבעי הוא Let me think about it and get back to you, אבל כאן עדיף פשוט להסכים.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine, but very minimal for an invitation. Show some enthusiasm.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל מינימלי מדי כתגובה להזמנה. כדאי להראות קצת התלהבות.

model_replies: Sounds perfect, count me in! Where should we meet?
Great, see you there. Should we meet outside?

practice.partner: Hey, are we still on for tonight?

options.text: Oh, I forgot to tell you, I'm not coming.

feedback.en: Cancelling at the last minute with no apology sounds careless. Say sorry and suggest another time.
feedback.he: ביטול ברגע האחרון בלי התנצלות נשמע לא אכפתי. כדאי להתנצל ולהציע מועד אחר.

options.text: I'm so sorry, something's come up and I can't make it tonight. Could we do next weekend instead?

feedback.en: Apologise, give a short reason and suggest a new time right away. It shows you still want to meet.
feedback.he: מתנצלים, נותנים סיבה קצרה ומציעים מיד מועד חדש. זה מראה שאתם עדיין רוצים להיפגש.

options.text: Sorry, I can't come today.

feedback.en: Polite enough, but without a new suggestion it can sound like you don't want to meet. Offer another day.
feedback.he: מנומס מספיק, אבל בלי הצעה חדשה זה עלול להישמע כאילו אתם לא רוצים להיפגש. כדאי להציע יום אחר.

model_replies: I'm so sorry, something's come up and I can't make it tonight. Could we do next weekend instead?
Really sorry, I have to cancel tonight. Can I take a rain check? How about next Saturday?

practice.partner: No worries! Next weekend works for me. I'll let the others know.

options.text: OK, thanks.

feedback.en: Fine, but after cancelling, a bit more warmth helps: 'Thanks for understanding.'
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל אחרי ביטול כדאי קצת יותר חום: Thanks for understanding.

options.text: Maybe. We'll see.

feedback.en: Sounds uncommitted right after you cancelled. Confirm the new plan clearly.
feedback.he: נשמע לא מחויב, ודווקא אחרי שביטלתם. כדאי לאשר את התוכנית החדשה בבירור.

options.text: Thanks for understanding. I'll text you during the week to set a time.

feedback.en: Grateful and committed: you take responsibility for the next step.
feedback.he: מכירים תודה ומראים מחויבות: לוקחים אחריות על הצעד הבא.

model_replies: Thanks for understanding. I'll text you during the week to set a time.
Thanks, Chris. Next weekend it is!

roleplay.persona: Chris, a classmate on the learner's semester in Boston. Easygoing and sociable, always organising group plans, but a bit vague about details.
roleplay.complication: Chris invites the learner for a night they can't make. After they agree on another day, Chris changes the time because of another friend, so the learner has to check whether it works, maybe suggest a different time, and confirm the final plan: day, time and place.
roleplay.opening_line: Hey! What are you up to on Friday night?

culture.en: In English, a direct 'No' to an invitation can sound unfriendly. People soften it ('I'd love to, but…') and suggest another time if they mean it.
culture.he: באנגלית 'לא' ישיר להזמנה עלול להישמע לא ידידותי. נוהגים לרכך (I'd love to, but...) ולהציע מועד אחר אם באמת רוצים.

culture.en: 'What are you up to on Friday?' often comes before an invitation. If you don't know the plan yet, answer 'Nothing much, why?' or 'Why, what's up?'
culture.he: השאלה What are you up to on Friday? באה הרבה פעמים לפני הזמנה. אם עוד לא יודעים מה התוכנית, עונים Nothing much, why? או Why, what's up?

culture.en: If you need to cancel, tell people as early as possible and apologise. Not turning up without a message is considered very rude.
culture.he: אם צריך לבטל, מודיעים כמה שיותר מוקדם ומתנצלים. לא להגיע בלי להודיע נחשב לחוסר נימוס חמור.

variants.us: go to the movies / movie theater
variants.note: 'Movie' is understood everywhere; 'film' is more British.
'Do you want to…?' is used everywhere.

scenarios.title_en: Making friends at a language exchange

situation.en: You're at a language exchange evening in a café in London. People pair up to practise each other's languages. Tonight you're practising with Ben, who is learning Hebrew.
situation.he: אתם בערב חילופי שפות בבית קפה בלונדון. אנשים מתחלקים לזוגות ומתרגלים זה את השפה של זה. הערב אתם מתרגלים עם בן, שלומד עברית.

goal.en: Introduce yourself, ask follow-up questions to get to know Ben, check words you don't understand, and swap contacts so you can meet again.
goal.he: להציג את עצמכם, לשאול שאלות המשך כדי להכיר את בן, לברר מילים שלא הבנתם ולהחליף פרטים כדי להיפגש שוב.

phrases.en: Hi, is this the language exchange?
phrases.he: היי, זה המפגש של חילופי השפות?

phrases.en: How long have you been learning Hebrew?
phrases.he: כמה זמן את/ה כבר לומד/ת עברית?

phrases.en: Why did you decide to learn it?
Your Hebrew is really good!
Sorry, could you say that again?
Could you speak a bit more slowly, please?
phrases.he: אפשר לדבר קצת יותר לאט, בבקשה?

phrases.en: What does 'knackered' mean?
phrases.note: Use this pattern for any new word. ('Knackered' is British slang for 'very tired'.)

phrases.en: How do you say this in English?
phrases.note: Point at something, or say the Hebrew word and ask.

phrases.en: Oh, interesting! What do you like about it?
phrases.he: אה, מעניין! מה את/ה אוהב/ת בזה?

phrases.en: Do you come here every week?
We should practise together again sometime.
phrases.note: UK spelling: 'practise' is the verb, 'practice' the noun. In the US, both are 'practice'.

phrases.en: Are you on Instagram?
phrases.note: Friendlier than 'Give me your Instagram'. Adding a reason ('so we can practise again') keeps it clearly friendly.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hi! Are you here for the language exchange?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yes! I'm Tal. I speak Hebrew, and I'm here to practise my English.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Perfect! I'm Ben, and I'm learning Hebrew. Shalom!

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Shalom! Your accent is really good. How long have you been learning?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: About a year. I have a class on Tuesday evenings.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Nice. Why did you decide to learn Hebrew?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: My grandma grew up in Haifa, and I've got cousins there.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Oh, that's so cool! Have you been to Israel?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Once, when I was a kid. I'm going again next summer.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Amazing. Do you come here every week?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Most weeks, yeah. It's my first time with a Hebrew speaker, though!

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Well, we should practise together again. Do you want to swap numbers?

practice.partner: Hi! Are you here for the language exchange?

options.text: Yes, I learn English since two years.

feedback.en: This follows Hebrew grammar. Use the present perfect with 'for': 'I've been learning English for two years.'
feedback.he: זה מבנה מהעברית. באנגלית משתמשים ב-present perfect עם for: I've been learning English for two years.

options.text: Yes! I'm Tal. I speak Hebrew, and I'm here to practise my English.

feedback.en: Friendly and useful: your name, your language, and what you want to practise.
feedback.he: ידידותי ושימושי: השם שלכם, השפה שלכם ומה אתם רוצים לתרגל.

options.text: Yes, I am. My name is Tal.

feedback.en: Correct, but add which language you speak and want to practise, so the exchange can start.
feedback.he: נכון, אבל כדאי להוסיף איזו שפה אתם מדברים ומה אתם רוצים לתרגל, כדי שהתרגול יוכל להתחיל.

model_replies: Yes! I'm Tal. I speak Hebrew, and I'm here to practise my English.
Yes, hi! I'm Tal, from Israel. I want to improve my English.

practice.partner: Perfect! I'm Ben, and I'm learning Hebrew. Shalom!

options.text: Shalom! That's great. How long have you been learning?

feedback.en: A friendly reaction plus a follow-up question about him.
feedback.he: תגובה חמה ושאלת המשך עליו.

options.text: Why? Hebrew is so hard and useless.

feedback.en: Discouraging and rude to someone who's making an effort. Show interest instead.
feedback.he: מייאש ולא מנומס כלפי מי שמשקיע. עדיף להראות עניין.

options.text: Shalom. I am Israeli.

feedback.en: Friendly, but it doesn't keep the conversation going. Ask him something.
feedback.he: ידידותי, אבל לא מקדם את השיחה. כדאי לשאול אותו משהו.

model_replies: Shalom! That's great. How long have you been learning?
Shalom! Wow, why did you decide to learn Hebrew?

practice.partner: About a year. My grandma grew up in Haifa, and I've got cousins there.

options.text: OK. I am from Tel Aviv.

feedback.en: Fine, but 'OK' sounds uninterested, and you change the subject to yourself. React first: 'Oh, cool!'
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל OK נשמע אדיש, ואתם מעבירים את הנושא לעצמכם. קודם מגיבים: Oh, cool!

options.text: Your grandmother is how old?

feedback.en: Unnatural word order ('How old is your grandmother?'), and a strange, personal question at this point.
feedback.he: סדר מילים לא טבעי (צריך How old is your grandmother?), וגם שאלה אישית ומוזרה בשלב הזה.

options.text: Oh, that's so cool! Have you been to Israel?

feedback.en: You react to what he said and ask a follow-up question. That's how conversations grow.
feedback.he: מגיבים למה שהוא אמר ושואלים שאלת המשך. ככה שיחה מתפתחת.

model_replies: Oh, that's so cool! Have you been to Israel?
Haifa! I love Haifa. Do you visit your cousins?

practice.partner: We had the best hummus in Haifa. Honestly, it was unreal.

options.text: Yes, yes.

feedback.en: Pretending to understand means you miss the chance to learn. At a language exchange, just ask!
feedback.he: להעמיד פנים שהבנתם זה לפספס הזדמנות ללמוד. במפגש חילופי שפות פשוט שואלים!

options.text: What?

feedback.en: Can sound rude. 'Sorry?' or 'Sorry, what does … mean?' is softer and tells him exactly what you missed.
feedback.he: עלול להישמע לא מנומס. Sorry? או Sorry, what does ... mean? רכים יותר ואומרים לו בדיוק מה לא הבנתם.

options.text: Sorry, what does 'unreal' mean here?

feedback.en: Perfect: you ask about the exact word. That's what a language exchange is for. (Here, 'unreal' means 'amazing'.)
feedback.he: מצוין: שואלים בדיוק על המילה. בשביל זה יש מפגש חילופי שפות. (כאן unreal פירושו 'מדהים'.)

model_replies: Sorry, what does 'unreal' mean here?
Sorry, could you say that again? I didn't understand 'unreal'.

practice.partner: Most weeks, yeah. It's my first time with a Hebrew speaker, though!

options.text: Well, we should practise together again! Do you want to swap numbers?

feedback.en: Natural and clearly friendly: the number is for a reason (practising).
feedback.he: טבעי וברור שזה ידידותי: המספר הוא בשביל מטרה (לתרגל).

options.text: OK. Goodbye.

feedback.en: Too cold, and you lose the chance to meet again.
feedback.he: קר מדי, ואתם מפספסים את ההזדמנות להיפגש שוב.

options.text: Give me your Instagram.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'Give me' sounds like an order. 'Are you on Instagram?' is friendlier.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל Give me נשמע כמו פקודה. Are you on Instagram? ידידותי יותר.

model_replies: Well, we should practise together again! Do you want to swap numbers?
Cool! Are you on Instagram? We could meet up and practise.

roleplay.persona: Ben, 22, a university student in London who is learning Hebrew because his grandmother grew up in Haifa. Enthusiastic, a bit nervous about his Hebrew, and very curious about life in Israel.
roleplay.complication: Ben talks quite fast and uses a couple of British expressions ('brilliant', 'I'm knackered'), so the learner has to ask him to slow down or explain. The learner should keep the conversation going with follow-up questions and suggest meeting again; Ben isn't on WhatsApp, so they need another way to stay in touch.
roleplay.opening_line: Hi! Are you here for the language exchange? I'm Ben.

culture.en: At a language exchange, asking 'What does that mean?' or 'Could you say that again?' is completely normal. Everyone is there to learn.
culture.he: במפגש חילופי שפות מקובל לגמרי לשאול What does that mean? או Could you say that again? כולם באו ללמוד.

culture.en: Swapping numbers or social media with new friends is normal. Linking it to a plan ('so we can practise again') keeps it clearly friendly.
culture.he: מקובל להחליף מספרים או רשתות חברתיות עם חברים חדשים. כשקושרים את זה לתוכנית (so we can practise again) ברור שמדובר בחברות.

variants.note: Spelling only.
'Gran' and 'nan' are British.

scenarios.title_en: At the pharmacy: describing symptoms

situation.en: You're travelling in London. You've had a bad cough for a few days, and since yesterday morning you've also had a sore throat and a fever. You go to a pharmacy to get something for it. You're allergic to penicillin. (This scenario is language practice, not medical advice.)
situation.he: אתם מטיילים בלונדון. כבר כמה ימים יש לכם שיעול חזק, ומאתמול בבוקר יש לכם גם כאב גרון וחום. אתם הולכים לבית מרקחת לקנות משהו שיעזור. יש לכם אלרגיה לפניצילין. (התרחיש נועד לתרגול שפה ואינו ייעוץ רפואי.)

goal.en: Describe your symptoms clearly, answer the pharmacist's questions (allergies, other medication) and understand how to take the medicine and when to see a doctor.
goal.he: לתאר את התסמינים בבירור, לענות על השאלות של הרוקח (אלרגיות, תרופות אחרות) ולהבין איך לקחת את התרופה ומתי צריך ללכת לרופא.

phrases.en: I've got a sore throat and a temperature.
phrases.note: 'Have a temperature' = have a fever. Very common in the UK.

phrases.en: I have a sore throat and a fever.
phrases.note: 'Fever' is understood everywhere.

phrases.en: I've had a cough for three days.
phrases.he: יש לי שיעול כבר שלושה ימים.
phrases.note: Present perfect + for/since, not 'I have a cough since…'.

phrases.en: It hurts when I swallow.
I feel really run-down.
phrases.note: 'Run-down' = tired and weak, usually because you're ill.

phrases.en: I'm allergic to penicillin.
I'm not taking any other medication.
Is there anything you'd recommend?
How often should I take it?
phrases.he: כל כמה זמן צריך לקחת את זה?

phrases.en: Do I need a prescription for this?
Can I take it on an empty stomach?
phrases.he: אפשר לקחת את זה על בטן ריקה?

phrases.en: Do you think I should see a doctor?
phrases.he: את/ה חושב/ת שכדאי לי ללכת לרופא?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Hi there, how can I help?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Hi. I've got a really sore throat, and I think I've got a temperature.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Oh dear. How long have you had the symptoms?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Since yesterday morning. And I've had a bad cough for a few days.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Is it a dry cough, or are you coughing anything up?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: It's mostly dry. It really hurts when I swallow, too.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: OK. Are you allergic to anything, or taking any other medication?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: No other medication, but I'm allergic to penicillin.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: That's fine, none of these contain it. I'd suggest paracetamol for the temperature and these lozenges for your throat.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Thanks. And how often can I take the paracetamol?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: The packet tells you how many to take and how often. Don't take more than it says. And if you're not feeling better in a few days, or it gets worse, see a doctor.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: OK, I will. Thanks so much for your help.

practice.partner: Hi there, how can I help?

options.text: My throat is hurting me very strong.

feedback.en: A word-for-word translation that doesn't work in English. Say 'I've got a sore throat' or 'My throat really hurts'.
feedback.he: תרגום מילולי שלא עובד באנגלית. אומרים I've got a sore throat או My throat really hurts.

options.text: Hi. I've got a really sore throat, and I think I've got a temperature.

feedback.en: Clear and specific: the pharmacist knows straight away what you need.
feedback.he: ברור ומדויק: הרוקח מבין מיד במה אתם צריכים עזרה.

options.text: I am sick. I need medicine.

feedback.en: Understandable, but too general. Describe your symptoms so the pharmacist can help.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל כללי מדי. כדאי לתאר את התסמינים כדי שהרוקח יוכל לעזור.

model_replies: Hi. I've got a really sore throat, and I think I've got a temperature.
Hi, I have a sore throat, a cough and a fever. Is there anything you'd recommend?

practice.partner: Oh dear. How long have you had the symptoms?

options.text: Two days.

feedback.en: A fine quick answer, but mention any other symptoms too. The more detail, the better the advice.
feedback.he: תשובה מהירה וסבירה, אבל כדאי לציין גם תסמינים נוספים. ככל שיש יותר פרטים, העצה טובה יותר.

options.text: Since yesterday morning. And I've had a bad cough for a few days.

feedback.en: Exact timing plus an extra symptom, with the present perfect ('I've had') used correctly.
feedback.he: תזמון מדויק ותסמין נוסף, עם present perfect (I've had) בשימוש נכון.

options.text: I have them since yesterday.

feedback.en: This follows Hebrew grammar. Use the present perfect: 'I've had them since yesterday.'
feedback.he: זה מבנה מהעברית. באנגלית משתמשים ב-present perfect: I've had them since yesterday.

model_replies: Since yesterday morning. And I've had a bad cough for a few days.
I've had them for about two days.

practice.partner: Are you allergic to anything, or taking any other medication?

options.text: No other medication, but I'm allergic to penicillin.

feedback.en: Answers both questions clearly. Always mention allergies.
feedback.he: עונים בבירור על שתי השאלות. תמיד מזכירים אלרגיות.

options.text: No, no problems.

feedback.en: Wrong answer: you are allergic to penicillin. Always mention allergies, even if you think they're not important.
feedback.he: תשובה שגויה: יש לכם אלרגיה לפניצילין. תמיד מזכירים אלרגיות, גם אם נראה לכם שזה לא חשוב.

options.text: I have allergy to penicillin.

feedback.en: Understandable, but the natural phrase is 'I'm allergic to penicillin' (or 'I have an allergy to…', with 'an'). Also answer the part about medication.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל הניסוח הטבעי הוא I'm allergic to penicillin (או I have an allergy to..., עם an). וכדאי לענות גם על החלק של התרופות.

model_replies: No other medication, but I'm allergic to penicillin.
I'm allergic to penicillin. I'm not taking anything else.

practice.partner: I'd suggest paracetamol for the temperature and these lozenges for your throat.

options.text: What is lozenges?

feedback.en: Asking is a good idea, but 'lozenges' is plural: 'What are lozenges?' (They're medicated sweets you suck for a sore throat.)
feedback.he: טוב ששואלים, אבל lozenges ברבים: What are lozenges? (אלה סוכריות לגרון עם חומר פעיל.)

options.text: Just give me the strongest thing you have.

feedback.en: Sounds demanding, and the strongest medicine isn't always the right one. Go with the pharmacist's advice and ask how to take it.
feedback.he: נשמע תובעני, והתרופה החזקה ביותר היא לא תמיד המתאימה. כדאי לסמוך על ההמלצה של הרוקח ולשאול איך לוקחים את התרופה.

options.text: Thanks. And how often can I take the paracetamol?

feedback.en: Checking how to take a medicine is smart, especially in a foreign language.
feedback.he: חכם לברר איך לוקחים תרופה, במיוחד בשפה זרה.

model_replies: Thanks. And how often can I take the paracetamol?
Great, I'll take both. How many can I take a day?

practice.partner: And if you're not feeling better in a few days, or it gets worse, see a doctor.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine, but as a visitor you may not know where to go. Ask.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל כתיירים אולי לא תדעו לאן ללכת. כדאי לשאול.

options.text: OK, I will. Where could I see a doctor around here, if I need to?

feedback.en: A useful follow-up: you're away from home and need to know your options.
feedback.he: שאלת המשך שימושית: אתם רחוק מהבית וצריכים לדעת מה האפשרויות.

options.text: I don't need doctor, I am strong.

feedback.en: Missing 'a' ('a doctor'), and brushing off medical advice isn't wise.
feedback.he: חסר a (a doctor), וגם לא חכם לבטל עצה רפואית.

model_replies: OK, I will. Where could I see a doctor around here, if I need to?
Thanks, I will. Thanks so much for your help.

roleplay.persona: Daniel, a calm, experienced pharmacist in a busy London pharmacy. Kind and thorough, he asks quite a few questions before he recommends anything.
roleplay.complication: The medicine the learner asks for first isn't suitable or needs a prescription, so Daniel asks follow-up questions (how long, how bad, allergies, other medication) and suggests an alternative. He advises seeing a doctor if things get worse, and the learner should ask where to go.
roleplay.opening_line: Hello there, what can I do for you today?

culture.en: In the UK, pharmacists can advise on minor illnesses, and many medicines are sold without a prescription. In an emergency, call 999 in the UK or 911 in the US.
culture.he: בבריטניה רוקחים יכולים לייעץ על מחלות קלות, ותרופות רבות נמכרות בלי מרשם. במקרה חירום מתקשרים ל-999 בבריטניה או ל-911 בארה״ב.

culture.en: Medicine names differ between countries: the same painkiller is 'paracetamol' in the UK and 'acetaminophen' in the US. Show the pharmacist the packet (or a photo) of your usual medicine.
culture.he: שמות של תרופות משתנים ממדינה למדינה: אותו משכך כאבים נקרא paracetamol בבריטניה ו-acetaminophen בארה״ב. כדאי להראות לרוקח את האריזה (או תמונה) של התרופה שאתם רגילים אליה.

culture.en: Always mention allergies and any medicine you already take, even if nobody asks.
culture.he: תמיד מציינים אלרגיות ותרופות שאתם כבר לוקחים, גם אם לא שואלים.

variants.note: The same medicine.
'I've got a temperature' (UK) = I have a fever.

scenarios.title_en: Lost passport: police report and embassy
scenarios.title_he: דרכון שאבד: דיווח למשטרה ופנייה לשגרירות

situation.en: You're travelling in Amsterdam and your passport is missing. You think you left it on a tram yesterday. Your embassy has told you they need a police report before they can issue an emergency travel document, and your flight home is in three days. (Procedures vary between countries; this scenario is for language practice.)
situation.he: אתם מטיילים באמסטרדם והדרכון שלכם נעלם. נראה לכם ששכחתם אותו בחשמלית אתמול. בשגרירות אמרו לכם שהם צריכים דיווח משטרה לפני שיוכלו להנפיק לכם מסמך נסיעה זמני, והטיסה הביתה בעוד שלושה ימים. (הנהלים משתנים ממדינה למדינה; התרחיש נועד לתרגול שפה.)

goal.en: Explain what happened, give the details the officer needs, explain why it's urgent and leave with a copy of the report and a reference number.
goal.he: להסביר מה קרה, לתת לשוטר את הפרטים שהוא צריך, להסביר למה זה דחוף ולצאת עם עותק של הדיווח ומספר אסמכתא.

scenarios.partner_role: police officer at the front desk

phrases.en: I'd like to report a lost passport, please.
phrases.he: אני רוצה לדווח על דרכון שאבד.

phrases.en: I think I left it on the tram yesterday afternoon.
phrases.he: נראה לי ששכחתי אותו בחשמלית אתמול אחר הצהריים.

phrases.en: I'm not sure if it was lost or stolen.
phrases.he: אני לא בטוח/ה אם הוא אבד או נגנב.

phrases.en: No worries, I can wait.
phrases.note: Relaxed but still polite, so it's fine with officials too.

phrases.en: It's an Israeli passport. The number is on this photocopy.
phrases.he: זה דרכון ישראלי. המספר מופיע בצילום הזה.

phrases.en: Could I get a copy of the report for my embassy?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל עותק של הדיווח בשביל השגרירות?

phrases.en: Is there a reference number?
My flight home is on Friday, so it's quite urgent.
phrases.he: הטיסה שלי הביתה ביום שישי, אז זה די דחוף.

phrases.en: Sorry, could you spell that for me?
phrases.he: סליחה, אפשר לאיית לי את זה?

phrases.en: What happens if someone hands it in?
phrases.he: מה קורה אם מישהו מוסר אותו?
phrases.note: 'Hand in' = give something you found to the police or staff.

phrases.en: I need an emergency travel document to get home.
phrases.he: אני צריך/ה מסמך נסיעה זמני (תעודת מעבר) כדי לחזור הביתה.
phrases.note: The general name for the temporary document an embassy can issue.

phrases.en: I'm calling to book an appointment at the consulate.
phrases.he: אני מתקשר/ת כדי לקבוע תור בקונסוליה.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Good morning. How can I help you?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Good morning. I'd like to report a lost passport, please.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: OK. When and where did you last have it?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yesterday afternoon. I think I left it on the tram, but I'm not completely sure.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Which tram, and roughly what time?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: The number 2, from the museum to Central Station, at about four o'clock.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Have you checked with the lost property office?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yes, I called them this morning, but nobody has handed it in.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: All right. Do you have any ID with you, or a copy of the passport?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Yes, here's a photocopy, and my driving licence.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Thank you. I'll write up the report now. You'll get a copy with a reference number.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Great, thank you. My embassy needs it urgently. My flight home is on Friday.

practice.partner: Good morning. How can I help you?

options.text: My passport is lost. Help me.

feedback.en: Understandable, but 'Help me' sounds desperate and like an order. 'I'd like to report…' is the standard phrase.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל Help me נשמע נואש וגם כמו פקודה. הניסוח המקובל הוא I'd like to report...

options.text: Good morning. I'd like to report a lost passport, please.

feedback.en: The standard, polite way to start. The officer knows exactly what you need.
feedback.he: הפתיחה המקובלת והמנומסת. השוטר מבין בדיוק מה אתם צריכים.

options.text: I lost my passport. You must find it!

feedback.en: Demanding sounds aggressive, and the police may not be able to find it. Ask to make a report.
feedback.he: דרישה כזו נשמעת תוקפנית, וייתכן שהמשטרה בכלל לא תוכל למצוא אותו. בקשו להגיש דיווח.

model_replies: Good morning. I'd like to report a lost passport, please.
Hi, I've lost my passport and I need to make a police report.

practice.partner: OK. When and where did you last have it?

options.text: I don't know where is it.

feedback.en: Word order: 'I don't know where it is.' In an indirect question, the subject comes before the verb. And try to give any detail you remember.
feedback.he: סדר מילים: I don't know where it is (בשאלה עקיפה הנושא בא לפני הפועל). וכדאי לתת כל פרט שאתם זוכרים.

options.text: Yesterday afternoon. I think I left it on the tram, but I'm not completely sure.

feedback.en: When, where, and how sure you are: exactly what the officer needs.
feedback.he: מתי, איפה ועד כמה אתם בטוחים: בדיוק מה שהשוטר צריך.

options.text: Yesterday. Tram.

feedback.en: The key facts are there, but it's too short. Use full sentences and say how sure you are.
feedback.he: העובדות החשובות שם, אבל קצר מדי. כדאי לדבר במשפטים מלאים ולהגיד עד כמה אתם בטוחים.

model_replies: Yesterday afternoon. I think I left it on the tram, but I'm not completely sure.
I last had it yesterday at about four. I think it fell out of my bag on the tram.

practice.partner: Have you checked with the lost property office?

options.text: No, it's your job to check.

feedback.en: Rude and unhelpful. The officer is giving you a useful tip. If you haven't checked, say 'Not yet. Could you give me the number?'
feedback.he: גס ולא מועיל. השוטר נותן לכם טיפ שימושי. אם עוד לא בדקתם, אמרו: Not yet. Could you give me the number?

options.text: Yes. Nothing.

feedback.en: Clear enough, but full sentences sound more cooperative.
feedback.he: ברור מספיק, אבל משפטים מלאים נשמעים משתפי פעולה יותר.

options.text: Yes, I called them this morning, but nobody has handed it in.

feedback.en: Shows you've already done your part, using the right phrase: 'hand in'.
feedback.he: מראה שכבר עשיתם את שלכם, עם הביטוי הנכון: hand in.

model_replies: Yes, I called them this morning, but nobody has handed it in.
Not yet. Could you give me their number?

practice.partner: Do you have any ID with you, or a copy of the passport?

options.text: Yes, here's a photocopy, and my driving licence.

feedback.en: You say exactly what you're handing over. Quick and clear.
feedback.he: אומרים בדיוק מה אתם מגישים. מהיר וברור.

options.text: Why you need it? I told you my name.

feedback.en: The question needs 'do' ('Why do you need it?'), and the tone is a problem: ID checks are routine, and arguing slows everything down.
feedback.he: בשאלה חסר do (Why do you need it?), וגם הטון בעייתי: בדיקת תעודה היא עניין שגרתי, וויכוח רק מעכב.

options.text: Yes. Here.

feedback.en: Fine, but tell the officer what you're giving them.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל כדאי להגיד לשוטר מה אתם נותנים לו.

model_replies: Yes, here's a photocopy, and my driving licence.
I've got a photo of it on my phone. Is that OK?

practice.partner: Have you contacted your embassy yet?

options.text: Yes. They want report.

feedback.en: Understandable, but missing 'a' and too short. 'They said they need a police report.'
feedback.he: מובן, אבל חסר a וקצר מדי. עדיף: They said they need a police report.

options.text: No, I'll go to the embassy after I find the passport.

feedback.en: If your passport is lost, contact your embassy as soon as possible; don't wait to find it.
feedback.he: כשדרכון אובד, פונים לשגרירות כמה שיותר מהר, לא מחכים שיימצא.

options.text: Yes, I called them this morning. They said they need a police report before they can give me an emergency travel document.

feedback.en: Clear and complete: the officer understands why the report matters. Note the reported speech: 'They said they need…'
feedback.he: ברור ומלא: השוטר מבין למה הדיווח חשוב. שימו לב לדיבור העקיף: They said they need...

model_replies: Yes, I called them this morning. They said they need a police report first.
Yes. They need a police report before they can give me a travel document.

practice.partner: I'll write up the report now. Is there anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Could I get a copy with a reference number? My embassy needs it, and my flight is on Friday.

feedback.en: You ask for exactly what you need and explain the urgency politely.
feedback.he: מבקשים בדיוק את מה שצריך ומסבירים בנימוס למה זה דחוף.

options.text: No, that's everything. Bye.

feedback.en: Polite, but you forgot the most important thing: a copy of the report for the embassy.
feedback.he: מנומס, אבל שכחתם את הדבר הכי חשוב: עותק של הדיווח בשביל השגרירות.

options.text: I need a paper for the embassy.

feedback.en: Understandable, but vague. Say 'a copy of the report' and ask for the reference number.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל לא מדויק. אמרו a copy of the report ובקשו גם מספר אסמכתא.

model_replies: Could I get a copy with a reference number? My embassy needs it, and my flight is on Friday.
Yes, could I have a copy of the report for my embassy, please?

roleplay.persona: Officer de Vries, a front-desk police officer in Amsterdam. Professional and fair, a bit tired at the end of a long shift; speaks clear but fast English.
roleplay.complication: The officer first suggests making the report online and coming back later. The learner has to explain politely that the embassy needs a signed report urgently because the flight is in three days. The officer then asks for exact details (when, where, passport number, an address in the city) and reads out a reference number with letters that the learner should ask to have spelled.
roleplay.opening_line: Good afternoon. What can I do for you?

culture.en: Before you travel, keep a photo of your passport's photo page on your phone and in your email. It makes reports and replacement documents much faster.
culture.he: לפני הנסיעה כדאי לשמור צילום של עמוד הפרטים בדרכון בטלפון ובמייל. זה מזרז מאוד דיווחים והנפקת מסמכים חלופיים.

culture.en: Embassies and consulates can usually issue an emergency travel document so you can get home. Requirements vary, so check your country's official consular website.
culture.he: שגרירויות וקונסולות יכולות בדרך כלל להנפיק מסמך נסיעה זמני (לישראלים: תעודת מעבר) כדי שתוכלו לחזור הביתה. הדרישות משתנות, ולכן כדאי לבדוק באתר הרשמי של משרד החוץ.

culture.en: Police officers in many countries speak English, but they'll appreciate short, clear sentences with the key facts: what, when and where.
culture.he: שוטרים במדינות רבות מדברים אנגלית, אבל הם יעריכו משפטים קצרים וברורים עם העובדות החשובות: מה, מתי ואיפה.

variants.note: 'Tram' is understood everywhere; some US cities say 'streetcar'.

scenarios.title_en: Phone stolen: getting help fast

situation.en: You're in central London. A man on a bike has just grabbed your phone out of your hand and ridden off. You're not hurt, but you have no phone. You need help from someone nearby, and then from the police.
situation.he: אתם במרכז לונדון. רוכב אופניים חטף לכם הרגע את הטלפון מהיד ונעלם. לא נפגעתם, אבל אין לכם טלפון. אתם צריכים עזרה ממישהו שנמצא בסביבה, ואחר כך מהמשטרה.

goal.en: Get a stranger's attention and ask for help, then report the theft clearly: what happened, when, where and what the thief looked like.
goal.he: לפנות לעובר אורח ולבקש עזרה, ואחר כך לדווח על הגניבה בבירור: מה קרה, מתי, איפה ואיך הגנב נראה.

scenarios.partner_role: a passer-by, then a police officer

phrases.en: Excuse me, sorry, could you help me?
Someone's just stolen my phone.
phrases.he: מישהו גנב לי עכשיו את הטלפון.
phrases.note: With 'just', British English often uses the present perfect.

phrases.en: Someone just stole my phone.
phrases.he: מישהו גנב לי עכשיו את הטלפון.
phrases.note: With 'just', American English often uses the past simple.

phrases.en: Could I borrow your phone to call the police?
phrases.he: אפשר להשתמש בטלפון שלך כדי להתקשר למשטרה?
phrases.note: 'Borrow' = take and give back. You borrow from someone; they lend to you.

phrases.en: Could you call the police for me?
phrases.note: Good when someone doesn't want to hand their phone to a stranger.

phrases.en: It happened just now, about five minutes ago.
phrases.he: זה קרה הרגע, לפני בערך חמש דקות.

phrases.en: He grabbed it out of my hand and rode off on a bike.
phrases.he: הוא חטף לי אותו מהיד וברח על אופניים.

phrases.en: He was wearing a black hoodie and a grey cap.
phrases.he: הוא לבש קפוצ'ון שחור וכובע מצחייה אפור.

phrases.en: He went that way, towards the station.
Is there a police station near here?
Could I get a crime reference number for my insurance?
phrases.he: אפשר לקבל מספר תיק בשביל הביטוח?
phrases.note: In the US, ask for 'a police report number' or 'a case number'.

phrases.en: I'm OK, just a bit shaken.
phrases.note: 'Shaken' = upset and scared after something bad happens.

model_dialogue.text: Excuse me, sorry, could you help me? Someone's just stolen my phone.

model_dialogue.text: Of course. Here, I'll put it on speaker so you can talk to them.

model_dialogue.speaker: you

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Which way did he go, and can you describe him?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: He went towards the station. He was wearing a black hoodie and a grey cap.

model_dialogue.text: OK, officers are on their way. Can you stay where you are?

model_dialogue.text: Yes, the officers will give you one when they get there.

practice.partner: Are you OK? What happened?

options.text: They stealed my phone!

feedback.en: 'Steal' is irregular: steal, stole, stolen. Say 'Someone stole my phone!' or 'Someone's just stolen my phone!'
feedback.he: steal הוא פועל חריג: steal, stole, stolen. אומרים Someone stole my phone! או Someone's just stolen my phone!

options.text: Someone's just stolen my phone. Could you help me?

feedback.en: Says what happened in one sentence, then asks for help.
feedback.he: אומרים מה קרה במשפט אחד, ואז מבקשים עזרה.

options.text: Phone! Stolen!

feedback.en: Understandable in a panic, but a full sentence helps people react faster.
feedback.he: מובן ברגע של לחץ, אבל משפט מלא עוזר לאנשים להגיב מהר יותר.

model_replies: Someone's just stolen my phone. Could you help me?
A guy on a bike just took my phone! Can you help me?

practice.partner: Oh no. Do you want me to call someone?

options.text: Give me your phone, quick!

feedback.en: Sounds like a demand, and the person may feel threatened. Ask: 'Could I borrow your phone?' or 'Could you call the police for me?'
feedback.he: נשמע כמו דרישה, והאדם עלול להרגיש מאוים. עדיף לבקש: Could I borrow your phone? או Could you call the police for me?

options.text: Yes, please. Could you call the police for me?

feedback.en: Polite and clear, and they don't have to hand their phone to a stranger.
feedback.he: מנומס וברור, והאדם לא צריך למסור את הטלפון שלו לזר.

options.text: Yes, the police.

feedback.en: Understandable in an emergency, but 'Yes, please' and a full request sound less like an order.
feedback.he: מובן במצב חירום, אבל Yes, please ובקשה מלאה נשמעים פחות כמו פקודה.

model_replies: Yes, please. Could you call the police for me?
Yes, please. Could I borrow your phone to call the police?

practice.partner: Is anyone hurt, and where are you right now?

options.text: I'm OK. I'm in the street.

feedback.en: Not specific enough. Name the street or a landmark nearby.
feedback.he: לא מספיק מדויק. כדאי לציין את שם הרחוב או מקום בולט בסביבה.

options.text: I don't know, I am tourist.

feedback.en: Missing 'a' ('I'm a tourist'), and you can still help: look for a street sign or a shop name.
feedback.he: חסר a (I'm a tourist), ואתם עדיין יכולים לעזור: חפשו שלט רחוב או שם של חנות.

options.text: No one's hurt. I'm outside the big bookshop on the corner, near the station.

feedback.en: Answers both questions and gives a landmark so they can find you.
feedback.he: עונים על שתי השאלות ונותנים נקודת ציון כדי שיוכלו למצוא אתכם.

model_replies: No one's hurt. I'm outside the big bookshop on the corner, near the station.
I'm fine. I'm on the main street, opposite the station.

practice.partner: Can you describe him?

options.text: Black clothes. Young.

feedback.en: Useful, but more detail helps: age, height, clothes, which way he went.
feedback.he: שימושי, אבל פרטים נוספים יעזרו: גיל, גובה, בגדים ולאיזה כיוון ברח.

options.text: He was about twenty, quite tall, and he was wearing a black hoodie and a grey cap.

feedback.en: Age, height and clothes, with the past continuous for what he was wearing.
feedback.he: גיל, גובה ובגדים, עם past continuous לתיאור מה שלבש.

options.text: He wear black hoodie and is tall.

feedback.en: Wrong tense and a missing 'a'. Say 'He was wearing a black hoodie, and he was tall.'
feedback.he: זמן שגוי וחסר a. אומרים He was wearing a black hoodie, and he was tall.

model_replies: He was about twenty, quite tall, and he was wearing a black hoodie and a grey cap.
Young, maybe twenty. Black hoodie, grey cap. He went towards the station.

practice.partner: Officers are on their way. Can you stay where you are?

options.text: Yes, I'll wait here. Will I get a crime reference number for my insurance?

feedback.en: You confirm, and you remember the reference number you'll need for insurance.
feedback.he: מאשרים, וזוכרים לבקש את מספר התיק שתצטרכו בשביל הביטוח.

options.text: No, I'm busy. Can you send me the report?

feedback.en: Leaving makes it harder for the police to help you. Stay, or explain politely why you can't.
feedback.he: אם תלכו, יהיה למשטרה קשה יותר לעזור לכם. הישארו, או הסבירו בנימוס למה אתם לא יכולים.

options.text: OK.

feedback.en: Fine, but ask about the crime reference number. You'll need it for insurance.
feedback.he: בסדר, אבל כדאי לשאול על מספר התיק. תצטרכו אותו בשביל הביטוח.

model_replies: Yes, I'll wait here. Will I get a crime reference number for my insurance?
Sure, I'll stay here. Thank you.

roleplay.persona: First Aisha, a passer-by who saw it happen: kind but in a hurry to catch a train. Then PC Hughes, a calm, efficient police officer who needs precise details.
roleplay.complication: Aisha is happy to help but nervous about handing her phone to a stranger, so the learner should ask her to make the call instead. PC Hughes asks for the exact location, the time and a description, and the learner needs to describe their own phone (model, colour, case). The learner should also ask about a crime reference number and how to block the phone.
roleplay.opening_line: Oh my goodness, are you OK? I just saw that guy grab your phone!

culture.en: In the UK, call 999 in an emergency (112 also works) and 101 for police matters that aren't emergencies. In the US, call 911.
culture.he: בבריטניה מתקשרים ל-999 במקרה חירום (גם 112 עובד), ול-101 לפניות למשטרה שאינן דחופות. בארה״ב מתקשרים ל-911.

culture.en: After a phone theft, use another device to lock or erase your phone through its find-my-device service, and ask your mobile provider to block your SIM.
culture.he: אחרי גניבת טלפון כדאי להשתמש במכשיר אחר כדי לנעול או למחוק את הטלפון דרך שירות איתור המכשיר, ולבקש מחברת הסלולר לחסום את כרטיס ה-SIM.

culture.en: Strangers are usually happy to help, but some won't want to hand their phone to someone they don't know. 'Could you call the police for me?' feels safer for them.
culture.he: אנשים זרים בדרך כלל ישמחו לעזור, אבל חלקם לא ירצו למסור את הטלפון שלהם למישהו שהם לא מכירים. Could you call the police for me? מרגיש להם בטוח יותר.

variants.note: Both also just say 'phone'.
With 'just', British English often uses the present perfect.
Spelling only.

scenarios.title_en: First day: meeting your new team
scenarios.title_he: יום ראשון בעבודה: היכרות עם הצוות

situation.en: It's your first day at a new job in a tech company in Tel Aviv. Half of your team works in London, so team meetings are in English. At the morning meeting, your team lead, Rachel, asks you to introduce yourself.
situation.he: זה היום הראשון שלכם בעבודה חדשה בחברת הייטק בתל אביב. חצי מהצוות יושב בלונדון, ולכן ישיבות הצוות מתנהלות באנגלית. בישיבת הבוקר ראש הצוות, רייצ'ל, מבקשת שתציגו את עצמכם.

goal.en: Introduce yourself in a few sentences (your role, your background, a hobby), answer friendly questions and ask one question back.
goal.he: להציג את עצמכם בכמה משפטים (התפקיד, הרקע ותחביב), לענות על שאלות ידידותיות ולשאול שאלה אחת בחזרה.

phrases.en: Hi everyone, it's great to be here.
I'm joining the team as a QA engineer.
phrases.he: אני מצטרף/ת לצוות בתור מהנדס/ת QA.
phrases.note: Say your job with 'as a' or 'as an': 'as a designer', 'as an analyst'.

phrases.en: Before this, I worked at a small start-up for three years.
phrases.he: לפני זה עבדתי שלוש שנים בסטארט-אפ קטן.
phrases.note: The job has ended, so use the past: 'I worked'. 'I have worked' would mean you still work there.

phrases.en: I'm really looking forward to working with you all.
phrases.he: אני ממש מחכה לעבוד עם כולכם.
phrases.note: After 'looking forward to', use the -ing form: 'to working', not 'to work'.

phrases.en: I'm still learning everyone's names, so please be patient with me!
phrases.he: אני עדיין לומד/ת את השמות של כולם, אז תהיו סבלניים איתי!

phrases.en: Sorry, could you remind me of your name?
phrases.he: סליחה, תוכל/י להזכיר לי איך קוראים לך?

phrases.en: What do you work on?
Who's the best person to ask about the test servers?
phrases.he: למי הכי כדאי לפנות בשאלות על שרתי הבדיקות?

phrases.en: Outside work, I love hiking and cooking.
phrases.he: מחוץ לעבודה אני אוהב/ת טיולים ובישול.

phrases.en: Thanks for the warm welcome.
Feel free to message me anytime.
phrases.he: אתם מוזמנים לכתוב לי מתי שרק תרצו.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you too!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Everyone, our new QA engineer starts today! Would you like to say a few words about yourself?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sure. Hi everyone, it's great to be here. Before this, I worked in testing at a small start-up in Haifa.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Welcome! How long were you there?

model_dialogue.speaker: you

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Oh, nice. So you know testing really well.

model_dialogue.speaker: you

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: That's totally fine, ask anything. And what do you like doing outside work?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I love hiking, and I'm learning to cook Thai food. Not very well yet!

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Ha! Well, we have a team lunch every Thursday, so you'll fit right in.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Sounds great, I'd love to come. Who's the best person to ask about the test servers?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
